heuristics.rule: CEC is the primary Express Entry pathway for PGWP holders already working in Canada
heuristics.condition: When an international student or worker is already in Canada with Canadian work experience
heuristics.action: Target the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) stream under Express Entry, not FSWP or FSTP
heuristics.because: CEC specifically rewards Canadian work experience, which PGWP holders accumulate; FSWP is designed for skilled workers outside Canada
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC Express Entry — Canadian Experience Class program definition

heuristics.rule: AC21 portability requires same-or-similar occupational classification after 180-day threshold
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B worker with an approved I-140 and a pending priority date changes employers
heuristics.action: The new role must be in the 'same or similar occupational classification' and the I-140 must have been filed before the priority date became current; change may occur after 180 days
heuristics.because: AC21 (American Competitiveness in the 21st Century Act) permits employer change without losing priority date only if these specific conditions are met
heuristics.regulatory_basis: American Competitiveness in the 21st Century Act (AC21)

heuristics.rule: PNP nomination adds +600 CRS points, effectively guaranteeing an ITA at the next draw
heuristics.condition: When a candidate's raw CRS score is below the general draw cutoff (typically 500+)
heuristics.action: Pursue a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) nomination to add 600 points to CRS score
heuristics.because: PNP nomination adds 600 points, which exceeds all recent general draw cutoffs and makes selection virtually certain
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS additional points — Provincial Nominee Program nomination

heuristics.rule: Layoff triggers a 60-day grace period for H-1B workers to find new employer or change status
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B worker is laid off or otherwise loses their position
heuristics.action: The worker has 60 days to secure new sponsoring employer or change to another valid status; priority date is not reset if I-140 was already approved
heuristics.because: USCIS regulations provide a 60-day grace period for H-1B nonimmigrants following involuntary termination; approved I-140 priority date survives independently of employment
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B grace period policy; AC21

heuristics.rule: BC PNP Tech stream can nominate eligible tech workers within 2 business days
heuristics.condition: When a tech worker holds an in-demand tech NOC code and has a job offer in BC
heuristics.action: Apply to BC PNP Tech stream as a priority pathway to the +600 CRS nomination
heuristics.because: BC PNP Tech stream specifically targets software, data, and IT management NOC codes and has a stated processing time of approximately 2 business days for nomination of in-demand codes

heuristics.rule: Under the wage-weighted lottery effective February 27, 2026, Level IV workers receive 4 lottery entries versus 1 entry for Level I workers
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B cap-subject petition is submitted under the wage-weighted lottery system (effective FY2027 cap)
heuristics.action: Employers and workers must classify the offered wage at the correct DOL prevailing wage level; Level IV classification yields 4x the lottery entries of Level I
heuristics.because: Federal Register document 2025-23853 (published December 23, 2025) establishes the wage-weighted lottery framework, disproportionately advantaging higher-wage workers in cap selection
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Federal Register document 2025-23853, published December 23, 2025; effective February 27, 2026

heuristics.rule: Candidate has exactly 60 days to submit full application after receiving an ITA
heuristics.condition: When IRCC issues an Invitation to Apply (ITA)
heuristics.action: Submit the complete permanent residence application within 60 days of ITA issuance
heuristics.because: The 60-day window is a hard deadline; failure to submit within this period results in the ITA expiring
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC Express Entry — ITA submission deadline

heuristics.rule: Cap-exempt H-1B petitions (universities, nonprofits) are not subject to the annual 85,000-slot cap
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B petition is filed by a qualifying cap-exempt employer such as a university or nonprofit research organization
heuristics.action: The petition proceeds to adjudication without entering the lottery; no cap registration required
heuristics.because: USCIS distinguishes cap-subject from cap-exempt petitions; cap-exempt approvals in FY2023 totaled 39,700 independently of the 85,000 cap-subject slots
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B cap-exemption policy; FY2023 Characteristics Report

heuristics.rule: Canadian PR holders must accumulate 730 days of physical presence in Canada per 5-year period to maintain PR status
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PR holder resides outside Canada (e.g., returns to home country)
heuristics.action: Track and ensure at least 730 days of physical presence in Canada within every rolling 5-year period
heuristics.because: Failure to meet the 730-day residency obligation (2/5 rule) risks loss of PR status

heuristics.rule: Canadian citizenship eligibility requires 3 years of physical presence out of 5 years after obtaining PR
heuristics.condition: When a PR holder is planning for long-term immigration security or circular mobility
heuristics.action: Accumulate 3 years of physical presence in Canada within a 5-year window to become eligible for citizenship application
heuristics.because: Citizenship removes the residency obligation and provides permanent right to return regardless of time spent abroad
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC — Canadian citizenship physical presence requirement

heuristics.rule: French language proficiency above CLB 7 in all areas adds +50 CRS points
heuristics.condition: When a candidate has French language skills above CLB 7 in all four language areas
heuristics.action: Submit qualifying French language test results (TEF/TCF) to claim additional 50 CRS points
heuristics.because: French language skills are an explicit additional-points category in CRS scoring and also unlock lower-cutoff French language proficiency draws
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS — additional points for French language skills

heuristics.rule: A job offer from a Canadian employer at NOC TEER 0 or 1 (senior management) adds +200 CRS points; other valid job offers add +50 points
heuristics.condition: When a candidate has a qualifying job offer from a Canadian employer
heuristics.action: Ensure the job offer is classified at NOC TEER 0/1 to claim the maximum +200 additional CRS points; otherwise claim +50
heuristics.because: The CRS point value of a job offer is directly tied to the NOC TEER classification of the offered position
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS — additional points for valid job offer

heuristics.rule: If you are an Indian national on H-1B with an approved I-140 in EB-2 or EB-3, treat your green card timeline as 50–100+ years under current policy, not as a near-term event
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national is planning their US stay assuming a green card will eventually arrive on a reasonable timeline
heuristics.action: Reframe the immigration timeline as effectively permanent temporary status and make career and life decisions accordingly
heuristics.because: With 525,000+ approved petitions and only ~40,000 visas available annually, the queue is structurally impossible to clear in a human lifespan under current law

heuristics.rule: If you've held a green card for fewer than 8 years, returning home carries no exit tax risk — timing the return before the 8-year mark is a meaningful financial lever.
heuristics.condition: When a green card holder is considering returning to their home country and has held the card for fewer than 8 of the last 15 years...
heuristics.action: ...model the return before crossing the 8-year threshold to avoid covered expatriate analysis entirely
heuristics.because: Exit tax only applies to those who held green card status for 8+ of the last 15 years; departing before that threshold eliminates exit tax exposure regardless of net worth

heuristics.rule: If your departure date is mid-year and your income is low in that partial year, withdraw from RRSP before leaving rather than after
heuristics.condition: When you are leaving Canada partway through a calendar year and your total Canadian income for that year will be below normal...
heuristics.action: ...make RRSP withdrawals before your departure date to be taxed at a lower marginal rate instead of the flat 25% non-resident withholding rate
heuristics.because: Once you become a non-resident, every RRSP withdrawal is subject to flat 25% withholding (no treaty reduction for India or China); partial-year Canadian income may put you in a lower marginal bracket, making pre-departure withdrawal cheaper

heuristics.rule: If you are an Indian national seeking a green card in the US, evaluate EB-1A or EB-5 first, not EB-2 or EB-3
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national is deciding which green card pathway to pursue
heuristics.action: Assess eligibility for EB-1A (extraordinary ability) or EB-5 (investor) before defaulting to employer-sponsored EB-2/EB-3
heuristics.because: EB-1A and EB-5 currently have no per-country backlog for India, meaning a 2–3 year or 4–12 month path versus a projected 134-year path

heuristics.rule: Never keep a green card 'just in case' without explicitly modeling the annual US tax compliance cost and worldwide income reporting obligation it creates.
heuristics.condition: When a returnee is tempted to retain their green card as an optionality hedge after relocating abroad...
heuristics.action: ...calculate the real cost: $2,000–$5,000/year in CPA fees plus potential US tax liability on home-country salary and investments, then decide deliberately rather than by default
heuristics.because: The IRS treats green card holders as US tax residents regardless of physical location, creating perpetual worldwide income reporting and FBAR obligations until formal abandonment via Form I-407

heuristics.rule: Stop all TFSA contributions on the exact date you leave Canada — not the end of the year
heuristics.condition: When you are departing Canada and becoming a non-resident for tax purposes...
heuristics.action: ...cease TFSA contributions immediately on departure date and do not contribute afterward
heuristics.because: Any TFSA contribution made while a non-resident triggers a 1% per month penalty on that amount; the penalty compounds monthly and is easy to accidentally incur if you have automatic contributions set up

heuristics.rule: Use O-1A as a bridge visa while building toward EB-1A if you are an Indian national stuck in H-1B dependency
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national wants to decouple their US work authorization from employer H-1B sponsorship and the EB-2/EB-3 queue
heuristics.action: Pursue O-1A classification to remove H-1B cap and lottery constraints while accumulating extraordinary ability evidence for EB-1A
heuristics.because: O-1A is renewable indefinitely, has no per-country backlog, and directly builds the evidentiary record needed for EB-1A self-petition

heuristics.rule: For Indian returnees, time large US retirement account withdrawals to fall within the RNOR window (first 2 years after return) to minimize combined US + India tax.
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national has returned to India and holds a 401k or IRA they plan to draw down...
heuristics.action: ...front-load distributions during the RNOR period when India does not tax foreign-source income, coordinating with the reduced US withholding rate under the treaty
heuristics.because: RNOR status shields foreign income from Indian taxation for up to 2 years; after that window closes, distributions may face double taxation without careful treaty planning

heuristics.rule: If you own Canadian real estate and plan to sell, sell before departure rather than as a non-resident
heuristics.condition: When you anticipate selling Canadian property within a few years of leaving...
heuristics.action: ...either sell before departing or budget explicitly for the buyer withholding 25% of the gross sale price (not profit) for months during clearance certificate processing
heuristics.because: The Section 116 withholding is on the full sale price — not the gain — creating a massive temporary cash flow gap; a $800K sale means $200K held by the buyer, which can take months to recover even if your actual tax bill is far lower

heuristics.rule: When modeling your US career trajectory as an Indian national, never count a future green card as a planning assumption unless you are on EB-1A or EB-5
heuristics.condition: When making long-term financial, career, or family decisions that assume eventual permanent residency
heuristics.action: Run your life plan assuming the green card never arrives and evaluate whether that plan still makes sense
heuristics.because: EB-2 India priority dates are at May 2012 — meaning even people who filed 12+ years ago are still waiting — making any forward projection speculative

heuristics.rule: Sell US real estate before departing rather than after, to avoid FIRPTA's 15% withholding on gross sale proceeds as a non-resident.
heuristics.condition: When a returning professional owns US real estate and is deciding whether to sell before or after relocation...
heuristics.action: ...sell before establishing non-resident status to avoid FIRPTA withholding obligations and associated compliance complexity
heuristics.because: Non-resident sellers face 15% withholding on the full sale proceeds under FIRPTA; selling as a resident avoids this withholding mechanism entirely

heuristics.rule: Do not over-contribute to RRSP in your final Canadian years if you plan to leave
heuristics.condition: When you know or suspect you will be leaving Canada within 1–3 years...
heuristics.action: ...limit RRSP contributions to amounts you can realistically draw down at favorable rates before departure or accept will be subject to 25% flat non-resident withholding indefinitely
heuristics.because: RRSP withdrawals as a non-resident from India or China face 25% withholding with no treaty reduction, meaning excess RRSP balances become a tax-inefficient asset compared to non-registered accounts where you have more exit flexibility

heuristics.rule: File Form W-8BEN with your 401k or IRA custodian to claim treaty-reduced withholding rates before taking any distributions as a non-resident.
heuristics.condition: When a non-resident former US employee begins taking distributions from a 401k or IRA...
heuristics.action: ...proactively file Form W-8BEN to claim the applicable tax treaty rate (e.g., 15% or zero for periodic payments under the US-India treaty) rather than accepting the default 30% withholding
heuristics.because: Custodians apply a default 30% non-resident withholding rate unless treaty benefits are explicitly claimed; failure to file results in overpayment that may require IRS refund claims

heuristics.rule: Maintain your Social Insurance Number records even after leaving Canada
heuristics.condition: When you have contributed to CPP over your Canadian working years...
heuristics.action: ...keep your SIN documented securely so you can eventually claim your CPP retirement pension from abroad
heuristics.because: CPP entitlements survive departure and can be paid to a foreign bank account, but the claim process requires your SIN; losing it creates bureaucratic barriers to recovering money you already contributed

heuristics.rule: Canadian PR holders have a realistic circular migration option that US Green Card holders do not — treat Canadian PR as an optionality asset, not just a residency status
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PR holder is considering returning to their home country for 2–5 years
heuristics.action: Model the circular path explicitly: return home, maintain 730-day requirement, preserve PR, then decide on citizenship later — rather than treating the decision as permanent
heuristics.because: Canadian PR only requires 730 days of physical presence in Canada over 5 years, making multi-year home-country stints structurally feasible in a way US Green Card status does not allow

heuristics.rule: If your annual savings in Canada drop below CAD $25,000/year, the financial case for staying over returning to a strong home-country career collapses in PPP terms.
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian-based professional is evaluating stay vs. return and calculating savings rate...
heuristics.action: ...treat CAD $25,000/year as the minimum threshold; below it, the home-country option deserves serious reconsideration on financial grounds alone
heuristics.because: Below this level, a senior professional in Bangalore/Hyderabad earning ₹50L+ can match or exceed Canadian savings in PPP-adjusted terms, eliminating the financial premium of staying

heuristics.rule: Returning with children aged 8–14 is the highest-risk window for educational and identity disruption
heuristics.condition: When a parent is considering returning to their home country with school-age children...
heuristics.action: ...treat the 8–14 age range as a red flag requiring a concrete school continuity plan before committing
heuristics.because: Social identity and educational track are most sensitive to disruption in this age range; children risk never fully adapting to either system

heuristics.rule: If your partner is the trailing partner in a return decision, model their career outcome independently before finalizing any plan.
heuristics.condition: When you are a dual-earner couple considering international relocation or return...
heuristics.action: ...assess your partner's career trajectory, network viability, and credential transferability in the destination country as a separate analysis from your own
heuristics.because: Research shows at least one partner suffers career interruption, status decline, or career relinquishment after relocation — and the trailing partner absorbs disproportionate damage

heuristics.rule: If a parent is 75+, eldercare pressure is no longer a future planning item — it is a current decision variable requiring active resolution now.
heuristics.condition: When your parent crosses 75 years of age...
heuristics.action: ...treat eldercare as an active, live factor in your career and location decisions, not a deferred concern
heuristics.because: After 75, care needs become highly variable and can escalate rapidly; waiting until a crisis forces the decision leads to worse outcomes than planning ahead

heuristics.rule: If you can't answer what you'd do if returning home felt wrong after 2 years, you haven't thought through the real risk
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a return-home decision...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly plan for the failure case before committing — identify what your next move would be if repatriation doesn't work
heuristics.because: People who can't imagine the failure case systematically underestimate reverse culture shock risk and get blindsided when it hits at months 6–12

heuristics.rule: Compare savings rate and PPP-adjusted net savings, not gross salary
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a US salary is financially superior to a home-country offer
heuristics.action: Build a line-by-line deduction model for both scenarios and convert to comparable units using PPP factors before concluding
heuristics.because: Gross salary comparisons systematically overstate the US advantage by ignoring taxes, housing, immigration costs, and purchasing power differences that can flip the outcome

heuristics.rule: Use sector-specific return viability, not generic 'career' comparisons
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to return to home country...
heuristics.action: ...first classify your sector into one of: Tech/AI, Finance (PE/VC vs. state), Academia, Medicine, Law/Government — because each has a different ceiling, income compression, and hiring market
heuristics.because: A framework that treats 'career' as one undifferentiated thing will give wrong answers for most people; the returnee premium, licensing friction, and competitive dynamics vary dramatically by field

heuristics.rule: Don't return to search — return to start
heuristics.condition: When planning a staged return to your home country
heuristics.action: Interview for home-country roles while still employed in the US, accept the offer before giving US notice, and negotiate a start date that allows unvested equity to vest
heuristics.because: Returning without employment puts you in a weak negotiating position — you're a returnee without current US anchor, under implicit time pressure, and perceived as less valuable than someone actively employed

heuristics.rule: Frame the decision as 10-year trajectory comparison, not current-conditions comparison
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to stay in host country or return home
heuristics.action: Rate each path on career compounding, financial compounding, immigration stability compounding, and relational compounding over 10 years — not on present quality of life
heuristics.because: Current-conditions comparison is biased toward staying because you are already adapted to the known environment; trajectories reveal which path actually compounds more value

heuristics.rule: Compare savings rate over 10 years, not gross salary numbers
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a US salary vs. a home country salary offer
heuristics.action: Model monthly savings after taxes, rent, and cost of living for both paths, then project net worth at 10 years
heuristics.because: A $200k US salary with $6k/month rent and 40% tax can generate less savings than a ¥30k/month salary in a Tier 2 Chinese city due to purchasing power differentials

heuristics.rule: Plan around immigration pathways that exist, not the one you're waiting for
heuristics.condition: When you are an Indian national on EB-2/EB-3 with a 50-100+ year backlog...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly plan around EB-1A, O-1, Canada PR, or return — not the backlog
heuristics.because: Waiting for a system that may never deliver converts a career decision into an indefinite limbo state with compounding personal and professional costs

heuristics.rule: If your savings rate in Canada in CAD is equivalent to your home-country savings rate in PPP terms, the financial case for staying in Canada is weak
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian-based professional is earning ~CAD $130K with ~$18,000–$20,000 annual savings
heuristics.action: Run a PPP-adjusted savings comparison against a concrete home-country offer before defaulting to 'staying is safer'
heuristics.because: The Canadian savings floor for mid-career tech professionals in Toronto is low enough (~$13,000–$15,000 USD/year) that home-country purchasing power may be comparable or superior

heuristics.rule: A single-income family in Vancouver or Toronto core on less than CAD $160K is effectively not building meaningful savings and should treat that as a structural problem requiring a fix, not a temporary condition.
heuristics.condition: When a single-earner household in a high-cost Canadian city runs the savings model and finds monthly savings under $1,000...
heuristics.action: ...immediately evaluate three levers: adding a second income, relocating to a lower-cost Canadian city, or reconsidering the return decision
heuristics.because: The Vancouver single-income model shows only $546/month savings on CAD $155K gross — housing alone consumes the surplus, and this arithmetic does not improve meaningfully with modest salary increases

heuristics.rule: If returning with young children, time the move before age 5 or after late high school
heuristics.condition: When a parent has children and is deciding when to return...
heuristics.action: ...structure the timing so children either form their primary identity in the home country (under 5) or are essentially launched in the US system (18+)
heuristics.because: These are the two windows where disruption is minimized; all windows in between carry meaningful developmental risk

heuristics.rule: If a 'take turns' compromise is agreed upon, require explicit written conditions and timeline before treating it as a real plan.
heuristics.condition: When dual-career partners agree that one will subordinate their career now in exchange for the other doing so later...
heuristics.action: ...define upfront the specific timing, trigger conditions, and what 're-emigration' actually means operationally
heuristics.because: Phase 2 re-emigration routinely gets deferred indefinitely in practice, converting a mutual agreement into a unilateral sacrifice and generating lasting resentment

heuristics.rule: If you have siblings already living in the home country, return for eldercare is rarely the only option — funded professional care plus frequent visits is a legitimate substitute.
heuristics.condition: When siblings are present in the home country and can share caregiving responsibility...
heuristics.action: ...model the option of remaining abroad while funding professional care and visiting 3–4 times per year before defaulting to return
heuristics.because: The presence of local siblings materially reduces the care gap that your physical return would fill; financial support from a US salary can fund care quality unavailable otherwise

heuristics.rule: Don't evaluate the return decision based on how home felt during the first 1–3 months back
heuristics.condition: When you've recently returned home and feel relief and excitement...
heuristics.action: ...suspend judgment on whether the decision was right until at least month 12
heuristics.because: Repatriation distress peaks 6–12 months post-return, after the honeymoon phase fades — early positive feelings are structurally misleading about long-term fit

heuristics.rule: 401k contributions are not liquid savings — treat them separately in the comparison
heuristics.condition: When calculating actual annual net savings in the US scenario
heuristics.action: Separate 401k balance from liquid savings; count it as a distinct long-term asset locked until 59½, not as spendable wealth
heuristics.because: Including 401k in net savings overstates short-term financial flexibility and conflates wealth accumulation with accessible capital

heuristics.rule: Compare net savings in PPP-adjusted terms, not gross income in nominal USD
heuristics.condition: When an income compression figure feels prohibitive...
heuristics.action: ...calculate actual annual savings in each scenario rather than comparing gross salaries, adjusting for cost of living
heuristics.because: A $400K US physician saving $80K/year may do worse in wealth accumulation than a Chinese physician earning ¥600K saving ¥300K/year in PPP-adjusted terms — the compression is real but must be measured against what you actually keep

heuristics.rule: Define pre-committed return conditions before they can shift forward
heuristics.condition: When you tell yourself 'I'll return eventually, after X'
heuristics.action: Write down specific, measurable milestones (title, liquid savings, named contacts, specific role) and treat them as binding triggers rather than aspirational targets
heuristics.because: Vague future conditions shift indefinitely — green card timelines extend, savings targets rise, and the person wakes up at 45 having never made a conscious choice to stay

heuristics.rule: Audit whether your stay decision is analysis or fear of failure in disguise
heuristics.condition: When you have concluded you should stay and are using career/financial arguments to support it
heuristics.action: Ask explicitly: 'Am I staying because this path genuinely compounds better, or because returning feels like admitting defeat?' If the honest answer is fear, the analysis is not done yet
heuristics.because: Fear of failure masquerading as career analysis is the primary distortion in this decision; catching it forces genuine evaluation rather than post-hoc rationalization

heuristics.rule: Adjust home country salary by 1.72x purchasing power before comparing to US income
heuristics.condition: When comparing nominal salaries between US and China
heuristics.action: Multiply Chinese salary by approximately 1.72 to get equivalent purchasing power, then compare to US take-home after taxes and cost of living
heuristics.because: China is approximately 72% cheaper than the US, meaning nominal salary comparisons systematically overstate the US advantage

heuristics.rule: Compare trajectories, not current conditions
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to return home versus stay in the host country...
heuristics.action: ...project what both locations look like in 5 years, not what they look like today
heuristics.because: The comfort of the known systematically overweights today's established life against an imagined difficult return, ignoring that the return destination is also growing and changing

heuristics.rule: Do not conflate 'stay in Canada' with 'stay in North America' — the Canada-vs-US decision and the Canada-vs-home-country decision require separate frameworks
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PR holder is dissatisfied with income or career trajectory
heuristics.action: First determine whether the issue is Canada specifically or North America generally; if it's income, the US comparison is the relevant one, not the home-country comparison
heuristics.because: Canadian tech salaries are 25–40% lower than US equivalents in USD, making the US a distinct and often superior third option that gets collapsed into 'staying' by default

heuristics.rule: Each $10K CAD increase in gross income yields only $5,500–$6,500 in additional net in Ontario/BC — use this to reality-check whether chasing a salary bump solves a savings problem.
heuristics.condition: When a professional in Ontario or BC is evaluating whether a salary negotiation or job switch will materially improve their savings rate...
heuristics.action: ...apply the 55–65% net yield rule to the gross increase before counting on it to close a savings gap
heuristics.because: High marginal tax rates in Ontario and BC mean the government captures 35–45% of each incremental dollar, so salary alone is a weak lever compared to housing cost reduction or adding a second income

heuristics.rule: Add $15,000–$50,000 per child per year to your financial model when returning to China or India
heuristics.condition: When a parent is modeling the financial case for returning to a home country with US-born children...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly budget international school fees as a recurring cost before comparing savings rates
heuristics.because: US-born children are typically excluded from or disadvantaged in public school systems in China and India, forcing families into expensive international school tracks

heuristics.rule: If partners are from different countries, evaluate third-country options (Singapore, Canada) before defaulting to either home country.
heuristics.condition: When one partner is Chinese and the other is Indian or from a third country, or when one partner is a US citizen and the other is not...
heuristics.action: ...analyze Singapore or Canada as genuine alternatives, not consolation prizes
heuristics.because: Immigration asymmetry in either partner's home country (limited work authorization for foreign spouses) makes third countries structurally cleaner for both careers simultaneously

heuristics.rule: If you are the only child, treat eldercare return as a near-certain future event and build your career and financial planning around it having a defined timeline.
heuristics.condition: When you are an only child with no siblings to share elder care responsibility...
heuristics.action: ...plan your career moves, financial compounding window, and immigration decisions with an explicit assumption that return will likely occur within 5–10 years
heuristics.because: There is no fallback option when you are the sole child; forced decisions made in crisis are reliably worse than planned transitions

heuristics.rule: If you're 40%+ likely to leave again within 5 years, treat the return option as having double transition cost
heuristics.condition: When calculating the true cost of returning home...
heuristics.action: ...factor in the realistic probability of a second international move and its associated career and life disruption
heuristics.because: The return-then-re-emigrate pattern is documented and common — ignoring it makes the return option look cheaper than it actually is

heuristics.rule: PPP adjustment applies only to local goods, not to USD-denominated or internationally priced items
heuristics.condition: When using PPP to make home-country savings look comparable to US savings
heuristics.action: Apply PPP only to food, domestic services, and local rent; keep international school fees, imported goods, US assets, and international travel at nominal exchange rates
heuristics.because: Overapplying PPP inflates the apparent value of home-country savings and produces an artificially favorable comparison for returning

heuristics.rule: Treat license incompatibility as a hard blocker, not a soft friction
heuristics.condition: When a professional in medicine or law is considering return...
heuristics.action: ...research exact re-licensing requirements before treating return as a viable near-term option
heuristics.because: US MD and US JD credentials do not transfer directly to Chinese or Indian clinical/legal practice; the re-qualification pathway is long, difficult, and conducted in a different language/legal system — it is a structural barrier, not merely administrative overhead

heuristics.rule: Build 3–5 specific home-country relationships who know your work quality before returning
heuristics.condition: When preparing for a staged return in any field
heuristics.action: Deliberately cultivate home-country network while still in the US through advising, conferences, consulting engagements, and LinkedIn thought leadership — not after arrival
heuristics.because: Returnees with a strong home-country network find roles in 1–3 months; those without one take 6–18 months and often return to the US in frustration

heuristics.rule: Treat a return at 25-28 with US credentials as elite positioning in home market, not failure
heuristics.condition: When framing return as giving up or losing
heuristics.action: Reframe: a top-university degree, 2-3 years of US work experience, English fluency, and an international network is premium positioning in most home markets
heuristics.because: The return-as-failure framing is imported from peers who are also afraid, not from realistic outcome assessment; the actual home-market value of those credentials is high

heuristics.rule: Treat total immigration legal costs as a direct compensation deduction
heuristics.condition: When calculating the real value of a US job offer requiring visa sponsorship
heuristics.action: Subtract $20,000–$100,000 in expected lifetime immigration legal costs from total US compensation before comparing to home country options
heuristics.because: These costs are paid directly from compensation and are invisible in standard salary comparisons, making the US offer appear more attractive than it actually is

heuristics.rule: Stage the decision: stay for a specific milestone, then return from strength
heuristics.condition: When the stay-vs-return decision feels binary and permanent...
heuristics.action: ...define a concrete career milestone (senior title, key technical experience, financial cushion) and treat it as a 3-5 year sprint with a deliberate return option
heuristics.because: Returnees with US credentials, senior titles, and savings enter home markets at a structural advantage over both domestic peers and over themselves had they returned earlier

heuristics.rule: Canadian citizenship should be evaluated as a passport asset, not just a residency endpoint
heuristics.condition: When an Indian or Chinese national is deciding whether to complete Canadian citizenship before returning home
heuristics.action: Calculate the visa-free access differential between a Canadian passport (185+ countries) and the home-country passport before deciding how urgently to obtain citizenship
heuristics.because: For Indian and Chinese nationals whose home passports have significantly restricted global mobility, Canadian citizenship is a durable travel and re-entry asset independent of where the person lives

heuristics.rule: The biggest single lever in Canadian savings arithmetic is dual income — adding a working partner at CAD $60K adds approximately CAD $40,000 in net household take-home.
heuristics.condition: When a single-income Canadian household is evaluating financial viability of staying...
heuristics.action: ...model the dual-income scenario explicitly before concluding that the finances don't work, because a second income changes the outcome more than any other variable
heuristics.because: The sensitivity analysis shows second income outranks housing optimization, province choice, and salary increases as an impact driver on annual savings

heuristics.rule: Reframe children's US citizenship as optionality, not a complication
heuristics.condition: When parents feel stuck because return seems to compromise their children's US future...
heuristics.action: ...treat the US passport as a retained option that keeps the decision reversible, not a reason to stay
heuristics.because: Children holding US citizenship can return to the US system at any point; the decision does not have to be permanent if the family retains that option

heuristics.rule: If a split-family arrangement is framed as 'temporary,' cap the planned duration at 6 months and build a hard decision point.
heuristics.condition: When one partner returns and the other stays in the US due to equity vesting, school schedules, or ongoing projects...
heuristics.action: ...treat any split-family arrangement beyond 6 months as a relationship risk requiring active management, not just logistical scheduling
heuristics.because: Research shows relationship quality declines significantly in split-family arrangements sustained beyond 6 months, and 'temporary' arrangements rarely self-resolve on planned timelines

heuristics.rule: Ask parents directly what they need and want before making a return decision on their behalf.
heuristics.condition: When eldercare is the stated or felt primary driver for returning...
heuristics.action: ...have an explicit conversation with parents about whether they want you to return or prefer you stay and succeed, and model the decision on their actual answer
heuristics.because: Many professionals are returning for their own peace of mind rather than for a parent's actual expressed need; surfacing the parent's preference distinguishes genuine care need from anxiety-driven decision-making

heuristics.rule: Use your last extended home visit (week 3 specifically) as a proxy for what living there will feel like
heuristics.condition: When assessing how well you'll readjust to your home country...
heuristics.action: ...recall how you felt by week 3 of your most recent extended trip home, not week 1
heuristics.because: Week 1 reflects novelty and honeymoon effect; week 3 reflects the underlying friction between your reshaped self and the home environment

heuristics.rule: If the two financial outcomes are within 10–20% of each other, stop optimizing the math and shift to non-financial variables
heuristics.condition: When a stay-vs-return model produces results that are close but not definitively one-sided
heuristics.action: Treat the financial question as resolved and make the decision on family proximity, career ceiling, reverse culture shock risk, and sense of belonging
heuristics.because: Within a 10–20% band, financial projections are within modeling error and life quality variables have larger actual impact on outcomes

heuristics.rule: In China, distinguish private-market roles from state-institution roles before assuming returnee premium applies
heuristics.condition: When evaluating finance or government opportunities in China...
heuristics.action: ...assess whether the specific role sits inside state-owned enterprises, state banks, or government — and if so, discount the returnee premium significantly
heuristics.because: Senior leadership in state-owned banks and government civil service tends to go to Party-connected domestic candidates; the returnee premium is real in PE/VC/tech but largely absent in state institutions

heuristics.rule: Frame return as a phase with evaluation conditions, not a permanent decision
heuristics.condition: When the psychological block 'if I return I can never come back' is delaying action
heuristics.action: Set a 2–3 year evaluation window with explicit criteria for whether the phase is working, and maintain awareness of re-entry options (remote work, third-country, return to US)
heuristics.because: Treating return as permanent causes either indefinite delay or desperate rushing before readiness; neither is optimal and re-entry options for US-experienced professionals are more available than assumed

heuristics.rule: Never let immigration inertia make the decision by default
heuristics.condition: When telling yourself 'I'll stay until I get my green card, then I'll think about it'
heuristics.action: Make a conscious, explicit stay-vs-return decision now, separate from the green card timeline
heuristics.because: Green cards take 5-20+ years for many nationalities; by the time it arrives, roots have deepened and the decision has been made by inaction rather than choice

heuristics.rule: If green card wait time exceeds 20 years, treat the US path as structurally capped
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national is evaluating long-term US career prospects
heuristics.action: Factor in 50–100+ year EB-2/EB-3 backlogs when assessing whether to stay, and quantify the opportunity cost of permanent temporary status
heuristics.because: Decades of 'temporary' status means decades of immigration tax, employer dependency, and constrained career mobility that compounding wealth projections rarely capture

heuristics.rule: Expand the option set before framing as stay-vs-return
heuristics.condition: When deciding between staying in the US and returning home...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate at least one third-country option (Canada, Singapore, UAE, UK) before making a binary choice
heuristics.because: Third geographies can solve simultaneously for career quality and immigration stability in ways neither the US nor the home country does at a given career stage

heuristics.rule: If your partner cannot get US work authorization but can work freely in Canada, that asymmetry overrides most income differential arguments
heuristics.condition: When a household is weighing Canada vs. US migration for income maximization
heuristics.action: Model household income, not individual income — if the partner earns freely in Canada but would be on dependent status in the US, the household total may favor Canada
heuristics.because: Dual-income households in Canada often offset the individual salary gap with the US; visa dependency for one partner in the US eliminates that offset

heuristics.rule: Use Toronto core vs. suburb as a $7,200–$10,800/year savings swing — if the job allows suburban living, this is the highest-return location decision available.
heuristics.condition: When a Toronto-based professional is optimizing savings without changing jobs or income...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate whether relocating from Toronto core to Mississauga/Brampton is feasible, since the rent differential alone recovers $600–$900/month
heuristics.because: Housing is the single highest-impact variable on Canadian savings rate, and suburban vs. core rent difference is achievable without a career change

heuristics.rule: China's dual nationality non-recognition effectively pre-makes a citizenship choice for the child
heuristics.condition: When Chinese nationals with US-born children are considering returning to China...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly map out the legal identity the child will carry in China and what that means for schooling, travel, and eventual citizenship choice
heuristics.because: China treats US-born children of Chinese nationals as Chinese nationals, creating legal ambiguity that affects school enrollment, university admissions, and exit travel

heuristics.rule: When a partner says they are 'supportive,' probe what they actually want independently before treating support as alignment.
heuristics.condition: When a user has modeled their own return economics in detail but describes their partner only as 'supportive'...
heuristics.action: ...ask what the partner's career trajectory looks like in the destination country in their own terms, separately from support for the primary earner's decision
heuristics.because: Stated support and genuine preference alignment are different things — unresolved misalignment surfaces after relocation when it is much costlier to reverse

heuristics.rule: If the urgency feels immediate but no acute health event has occurred, treat the feeling as future anxiety, not a current care requirement.
heuristics.condition: When the return impulse is driven by worry about what might happen rather than what is currently happening...
heuristics.action: ...separately model what a planned response to a future crisis would look like, rather than acting on anticipatory anxiety as if it were a present crisis
heuristics.because: Anticipatory anxiety and actual care need produce the same emotional urgency but have different correct responses; conflating them leads to premature decisions

heuristics.rule: Seek out returnees who came back 3–5 years ago, not those who returned recently
heuristics.condition: When gathering social proof about the return experience...
heuristics.action: ...specifically talk to people 3–5 years post-return, not people in their first year back
heuristics.because: People in the honeymoon phase give misleadingly positive signals; those at year 3–5 have lived through the peak distress period and can give calibrated feedback

heuristics.rule: Include immigration legal fees as a recurring annual cost in the US scenario, not a one-time expense
heuristics.condition: When comparing ongoing cost of living in the US during H-1B or green card processing years
heuristics.action: Add $5,000–$15,000/year for immigration legal costs to the US deduction column as a recurring line item
heuristics.because: These fees are paid annually during the multi-year H-1B and green card process and materially reduce net savings but are routinely omitted from comparisons

heuristics.rule: For academia returnees to China, evaluate the field-specific academic freedom constraint before accepting recruitment packages
heuristics.condition: When a US-trained academic in social sciences, humanities, or politically sensitive STEM is considering Chinese talent programs...
heuristics.action: ...weight academic freedom constraints heavily, not just the financial package
heuristics.because: China's recruitment packages are financially genuine, but research freedom in social sciences, humanities, and dual-use STEM fields is materially constrained — the package value is diminished if it limits research agenda

heuristics.rule: Wait for a major vesting event before departing
heuristics.condition: When you have unvested equity at a US company and a return offer in hand
heuristics.action: Negotiate your home-country start date to allow the vesting event to complete before giving US notice
heuristics.because: Unvested equity is a concrete financial asset that is permanently forfeited on early departure — it is a quantifiable cost of unplanned timing

heuristics.rule: Compare savings rate, not gross salary
heuristics.condition: When doing financial comparison between staying and returning
heuristics.action: Adjust gross income for taxes, cost of living, immigration legal costs, family remittances, and purchasing power before comparing
heuristics.because: $200k in San Francisco saving $30k/year is not clearly superior to ¥40k/month in Shanghai saving ¥25k/month while living rent-free near family

heuristics.rule: Count immigration overhead as 20–100 hours per year in your time budget
heuristics.condition: When a visa-holding professional is evaluating work-life quality in the US
heuristics.action: Explicitly account for time spent on visa tracking, attorney coordination, renewal trips, and mental overhead as a recurring annual cost
heuristics.because: This cognitive and time load is real, affects work and life quality, and is never included in salary or lifestyle comparisons

heuristics.rule: Treat US startup founding as structurally blocked on a work visa
heuristics.condition: When entrepreneurship is part of your long-term plan and you are on an H-1B or similar work visa...
heuristics.action: ...factor in that founding requires either leaving visa status, obtaining O-1/EB-1A, or navigating a multi-year NIW process — and weight return or third-country options accordingly
heuristics.because: At home, there are no immigration constraints on entrepreneurship; the cost of a failed startup is far lower without visa consequences, and many successful founders from India and China built companies after returning specifically because returning removed these constraints

heuristics.rule: Track your 730-day physical presence window actively from the day you receive PR — not when you're planning a long trip
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PR holder begins making extended home-country visits or considering a return
heuristics.action: Use Service Canada's travel history tool to calculate remaining days in the current 5-year window before booking any extended absence
heuristics.because: PR holders who don't track proactively often discover they've inadvertently jeopardized their status only when questioned at the border on return

heuristics.rule: For academia, longer US tenure directly increases home-country negotiating leverage
heuristics.condition: When an academic is evaluating how long to stay in the US before returning
heuristics.action: Stay long enough to accumulate publications and reputation because home-country universities are specifically recruiting for that credential
heuristics.because: The staged return is best aligned with academia — the longer the stay with demonstrated output, the stronger the startup fund, salary supplement, and housing package you can negotiate on return

heuristics.rule: Expand the option set beyond binary stay-vs-hometown before deciding
heuristics.condition: When the decision feels like a forced choice between staying indefinitely or returning to hometown
heuristics.action: Explicitly evaluate: return with a plan at 28, third-country options (Canada, Singapore, UK, Dubai), split-life arrangements, or delayed return after hitting a specific milestone
heuristics.because: Binary framing forecloses legitimate paths that may dominate both default options on multiple dimensions

heuristics.rule: Only pursue US path if targeting elite outcomes; for median outcomes, the ROI case weakens significantly
heuristics.condition: When an international student is modeling whether the $400k–$800k total investment in US education and immigration pays off
heuristics.action: Benchmark your realistic career outcome against the median, not the FAANG ceiling, before committing to the US path
heuristics.because: The investment compounds favorably for elite destinations (FAANG, top finance, top research) but often does not beat a career that started earlier at home for median outcomes

heuristics.rule: Returning professionals should not self-assess as junior candidates in home markets
heuristics.condition: When a professional with 5+ years at a US tech company considers returning home...
heuristics.action: ...enter the home market at senior levels with explicit expectation of startup equity and leadership roles
heuristics.because: International education, English fluency, cross-cultural experience, and knowledge of global best practices are scarce and carry a specific returnee premium in markets trying to scale internationally

heuristics.rule: Account for windows that close when sizing the urgency of the return option
heuristics.condition: When assuming the return option is always available and can be deferred indefinitely
heuristics.action: Identify which home-market opportunities (entrepreneurship, social capital formation, family relationships) are time-sensitive and assess how much narrower those windows become each year you stay
heuristics.because: Returning at 25 is categorically different from returning at 40; the entrepreneurial opportunity, the social capital needed to start a company, and the family relationships you can still influence shrink with each passing year

heuristics.rule: Seek out returnees in your network before deciding, not just stayers
heuristics.condition: When using your social network as evidence that staying is correct
heuristics.action: Actively identify and talk to people from your cohort who returned and are doing well
heuristics.because: Peer groups self-select around shared decisions; people who return are systematically underrepresented in your local social network, creating a survivorship-bias illusion that staying is the dominant choice

heuristics.rule: French bilingual route is the single biggest CRS lever for candidates already above CLB 10 in English
heuristics.condition: When a candidate is stuck below 470 CRS and has already maximized English language scores
heuristics.action: Pursue TEF Canada at B1 level via 3-6 months of structured study before attempting other optimizations
heuristics.because: Post author gained +50 points from French alone; top comment (445 upvotes) corroborates that TEF Canada is more lenient than DELF and B1 is achievable in that timeframe for English speakers

heuristics.rule: For Indian nationals in CS, Canada's Express Entry is almost always faster to permanent residency than the US EB-2/EB-3 track
heuristics.condition: When an Indian national in a skilled occupation is choosing between US H-1B → green card vs. Canada PGWP → PR
heuristics.action: Default to Canada track unless there is a specific, concrete reason the US path is faster (e.g., EB-1A, O-1, or employer-sponsored EB-1C with real timeline)
heuristics.because: EB-2 India priority date is currently ~2012-2013, implying 40+ year wait; Canadian PR via Express Entry typically takes 6-12 months from ITA to landing, as confirmed by the poster and corroborated by upvoted comments

heuristics.rule: Set a fixed schedule for checking IRCC portal status rather than checking daily or multiple times per day
heuristics.condition: When waiting for immigration decisions or draw results and experiencing anxiety from uncertainty
heuristics.action: Limit portal checks to once per week on a fixed schedule
heuristics.because: Multiple top-voted comments (234, 198 upvotes) corroborate that constant checking amplifies anxiety without adding actionable information — the information density per check is near zero during wait periods

heuristics.rule: Apply for PGWP within 180 days of receiving final marks/transcript — do not wait for the physical degree parchment
heuristics.condition: When a student has completed their program and is eligible for PGWP...
heuristics.action: Submit PGWP application as soon as official transcript or registrar completion letter is available, not when the physical degree arrives
heuristics.because: IRCC has denied PGWP applications from people who waited beyond the 180-day window believing they had more time; the clock starts from final marks, not convocation ceremony

heuristics.rule: State your PGWP status explicitly and proactively, clarifying no sponsorship is needed
heuristics.condition: When applying for Canadian tech jobs on a PGWP...
heuristics.action: Include a clear statement such as 'I hold an open work permit (PGWP) valid until [date]. No current or future sponsorship required for PR purposes.' — ideally bolded at the top of your resume and in your intro
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters (267 and 145 upvotes) confirmed that Canadian employers frequently confuse 'work permit' with 'requires sponsorship,' causing applications to be screened out before review

heuristics.rule: Frame PGWP as 'no employer action required' — not as a sponsorship ask
heuristics.condition: When applying to Canadian employers as a PGWP holder...
heuristics.action: State explicitly in work authorization fields: 'Open Work Permit (PGWP) — authorized to work for any employer in Canada. No sponsorship required.'
heuristics.because: PGWP is an open work permit owned by the worker, not tied to an employer — framing it as sponsorship creates a false burden that does not exist

heuristics.rule: Don't raise visa sponsorship in a phone screen unless directly asked
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student on OPT in early-stage interview rounds (phone screen)...
heuristics.action: Wait until onsite or final rounds to proactively raise the sponsorship question
heuristics.because: Raising it too early signals anxiety and filters you out before the company has invested in evaluating you — multiple commenters and the OP converged on this timing rule

heuristics.rule: Never mention visa status or sponsorship needs in the first outreach email
heuristics.condition: When an international student on OPT/H-1B is cold emailing a potential employer for the first time
heuristics.action: Omit all visa and sponsorship language from the initial email; surface it only once a genuine two-way conversation has developed
heuristics.because: Multiple high-upvoted comments (456, 176 upvotes) confirm that opening with sponsorship needs triggers immediate rejection before the reader evaluates skills — delaying the disclosure until interest is established inverts the rejection dynamic

heuristics.rule: Check the advisor's industry internship placement record before choosing a PhD program for an industry research track
heuristics.condition: When a student is aiming for research scientist or applied scientist roles at tech companies...
heuristics.action: Ask during campus visits: 'Where did your students intern? Which ones ended up at industry labs?' Then verify on LinkedIn.
heuristics.because: Multiple high-upvote comments (987, 312) corroborate that the advisor's industry network and internship pipeline determines industry placement more than program ranking or advisor h-index

heuristics.rule: Get H-1B sponsorship commitment in writing before accepting an offer
heuristics.condition: When accepting a job offer that requires H-1B sponsorship...
heuristics.action: Request explicit written language in the offer letter, e.g. 'Company will file H-1B petition on employee's behalf for the next available cap season,' before signing
heuristics.because: Multiple high-voted comments (287, 198 upvotes) confirm that verbal promises are not legally binding for H-1B sponsorship and companies can rescind without consequence

heuristics.rule: The 60-day grace period is a transition window, not a work window — treat it as departure/status-change time only
heuristics.condition: When your F-1 authorized stay ends (program end date or OPT authorization ends)
heuristics.action: Use the 60 days to file for a new status, transfer to a new school, or prepare to depart — do not attempt to work
heuristics.because: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(iv) explicitly prohibits work during this period; it is for transitioning out of status, not continuing employment

heuristics.rule: If your goal is long-term US immigration, avoid Day 1 CPT schools regardless of short-term work authorization need
heuristics.condition: When an F-1 student is considering a Day 1 CPT school primarily to gain immediate work authorization
heuristics.action: Do not enroll in Day 1 CPT programs if long-term US immigration is the goal
heuristics.because: The short-term authorization gain is outweighed by potential retroactive unlawful presence findings, RFEs at H-1B stage, and consular red flags — multiple commenters and the original poster corroborate this risk-reward asymmetry

heuristics.rule: If you have a US master's degree, always register for the master's cap pool, not just the regular cap
heuristics.condition: When an F-1 student with a US master's degree is registering for H-1B lottery...
heuristics.action: Register for the 20k master's cap pool in addition to (or instead of) the general 65k cap pool
heuristics.because: The master's cap is a separate, smaller pool with better per-registrant odds — multiple commenters confirmed this and noted people miss it even from top programs

heuristics.rule: After two consecutive H-1B lottery losses with expiring STEM OPT, consult an immigration attorney about cap-exempt employer options before assuming you must leave
heuristics.condition: When an F-1 holder has lost the H-1B lottery twice and STEM OPT expiration is approaching...
heuristics.action: Engage an immigration attorney to evaluate whether a cap-exempt dual-employment arrangement is structurally viable for your specific situation
heuristics.because: The post author explicitly used this strategy after two losses, and a corroborating commenter (134 upvotes) confirmed doing the same for two years through a university collaboration — establishing this as a real, repeatable path rather than a one-off

heuristics.rule: Check H-1B sponsorship history before targeting a company for an internship
heuristics.condition: When evaluating internship targets as an international student on F-1...
heuristics.action: Use H1Bdata.info or MyVisaJobs to verify the company files H-1B petitions; treat any company with fewer than 5 H-1B filings per year as high risk and deprioritize
heuristics.because: An internship at a company that won't sponsor leads to a return offer with no path to H-1B — wasting the best conversion opportunity available to international students

heuristics.rule: Build a Plan B you would genuinely choose, not just tolerate
heuristics.condition: When facing H-1B lottery uncertainty or any high-stakes immigration outcome...
heuristics.action: Actively research, visit, and emotionally invest in your backup option (e.g., Canada PR, another country) so it feels like a real path, not a fallback
heuristics.because: Multiple high-upvote comments confirm that genuinely accepting an alternative option reduced desperation and made the primary outcome feel less catastrophic either way — corroborated by rank=4 comment and rank=11 top comment (167 upvotes)

heuristics.rule: STEM graduates should stay in the US for at least 3–6 years before deciding to return
heuristics.condition: When you are a STEM graduate with a job offer at a reputable US company (e.g., Silicon Valley tech firm)
heuristics.action: Stay in the US for 3–6 years to accumulate savings, repay tuition, and build internationally recognized experience
heuristics.because: The poster calculates that a $70–80k salary allows repaying study-abroad tuition within 2–3 years, plus building a down payment — outcomes not achievable on Chinese domestic graduate salaries in the same timeframe; 29-month STEM OPT extension provides a real window

heuristics.rule: Match your job search to companies that have business connections to the country where you studied
heuristics.condition: When a returning student is trying to leverage their overseas study experience in the Chinese job market...
heuristics.action: Target companies with cross-border operations or business in the region where you studied rather than purely domestic firms
heuristics.because: The post argues that the absolute competitive advantage of returnees exists precisely in companies with overseas business ties — illustrated by the example of a student who worked in an Indian restaurant in the UK and leveraged that cultural exposure to land a job at Kuaishou handling India-market operations

heuristics.rule: High income does not guarantee life satisfaction — cultural belonging and social texture matter as much as compensation
heuristics.condition: When a person earns top-5% US income but lacks genuine social integration with local culture
heuristics.action: Evaluate social and cultural fit explicitly before treating income as the dominant decision variable
heuristics.because: Sample 1 (top-5% earner, $700K+) describes persistent unhappiness, mild depression, and a sense of meaninglessness despite financial success, while Sample 3 earns less than half as much but describes himself as extremely happy due to rich social and recreational life

heuristics.rule: Return before 35 or don't bother
heuristics.condition: When considering returning to China after living in the US for an extended period...
heuristics.action: Return before age 35, otherwise lifestyle habits are too entrenched to readjust
heuristics.because: The top answer explicitly states that returning after 35 means suffering because life habits can no longer be changed — the person has been acculturated too deeply

heuristics.rule: Sort your priorities by heart, not by head, before comparing countries
heuristics.condition: When deciding between staying abroad and returning home and feeling paralyzed by the comparison...
heuristics.action: Explicitly rank what you actually care about (income, family, adventure, entrepreneurship, stability) in priority order before doing any numerical comparison
heuristics.because: The commenter who returned to Shanghai describes ranking priorities 'by heart, not head' as the step that made the answer obvious — the country comparison only becomes meaningful after you know your own ordering

heuristics.rule: Before deciding to return, build a complete plan covering what you will do, what difficulties you will face, what costs are involved, and what risks you will bear
heuristics.condition: When considering returning to home country without a concrete roadmap
heuristics.action: Delay the return decision until you can answer all four planning questions concretely
heuristics.because: Commenter explicitly states that returning without this plan is 'blind' — the decision becomes arbitrary without grounded answers to these questions

heuristics.rule: Improving English IELTS beyond CLB 10 has diminishing returns and should be deprioritized
heuristics.condition: When a candidate is already at CLB 10 and is considering retaking IELTS to gain points
heuristics.action: Redirect that effort to French or spouse language score instead
heuristics.because: Post author explicitly reported only ~6 marginal points gained from CLB 10 to CLB 11, making it a low-ROI activity relative to other levers

heuristics.rule: Use PNPs as a backdoor when federal CRS score is not clearing draws
heuristics.condition: When an Express Entry candidate's CRS score is below the threshold for recent federal draws
heuristics.action: Actively monitor and apply to aggressive PNP streams (e.g., Alberta, Saskatchewan) which can add 600 points to CRS via nomination
heuristics.because: Poster explicitly identified PNPs as a 'genuine backdoor' and cited Alberta and Saskatchewan as aggressive programs; this point received engagement without contradiction

heuristics.rule: Research your Plan B concretely rather than leaving it as an abstract catastrophic scenario
heuristics.condition: When the prospect of returning home feels paralyzing or catastrophic
heuristics.action: Actually research realistic opportunity, salary, and life quality in the home country in specific terms
heuristics.because: Multiple comments (upvotes 198, 176) corroborate that abstractly fearing Plan B inflates its negative valence — concrete research consistently made it feel less catastrophic and reduced desperation driving bad decisions

heuristics.rule: Use the official registrar completion letter as proof of graduation — not a program completion email from a professor or department
heuristics.condition: When assembling PGWP application documents...
heuristics.action: Obtain and submit the convocation/completion letter issued by the registrar's office specifically
heuristics.because: IRCC requires the official registrar document; informal communications from faculty are not accepted as equivalent proof

heuristics.rule: Target mid-size companies (50–200 employees) over large tech companies when job searching as a PGWP holder
heuristics.condition: When beginning a Canadian tech job search on PGWP...
heuristics.action: Prioritize companies in the 50–200 employee range in tech corridors like Toronto/Waterloo rather than applying to Shopify, Amazon, Google, or other large employers
heuristics.because: Large Canadian tech companies receive flooded application volumes; mid-size companies are more receptive — corroborated by original poster's experience and a 167-upvote comment confirming the same pattern

heuristics.rule: Prioritize IELTS/TEF prep early — language scores are the highest-ROI lever for CRS
heuristics.condition: When planning your Express Entry strategy after getting your PGWP...
heuristics.action: Start language test preparation before or immediately after graduation, targeting both English (IELTS) and French (TEF/TCF) if any French background exists
heuristics.because: French scores can add 25-50+ CRS points, which is a larger marginal gain than most other factors within a graduate's control; multiple commenters with high upvotes corroborated this

heuristics.rule: Clarify what 'no sponsorship' means before self-eliminating
heuristics.condition: When a company says 'we don't sponsor visas'...
heuristics.action: Ask whether that applies to OPT and STEM OPT extension, or only H-1B — many companies mean only H-1B when they say 'no sponsorship'
heuristics.because: A commenter with 198 upvotes noted that some companies saying 'no sponsorship' will still do STEM OPT extension forms, and a 176-upvote comment confirmed a recruiter who said 'we don't sponsor' reversed course once OPT was explained

heuristics.rule: Target the hiring manager on LinkedIn, not HR or recruiter
heuristics.condition: When doing cold outreach for a software engineering or technical role
heuristics.action: Find and email the direct hiring manager rather than HR or a recruiter
heuristics.because: A 176-upvote comment explicitly states managers hire to solve a problem while HR screens for quotas — the conversations and incentives are fundamentally different, and HR is more likely to filter on sponsorship criteria before forwarding

heuristics.rule: Do not pursue a funded PhD if your end goal is a pure software engineering role
heuristics.condition: When a CS/ML student is considering a PhD but ultimately wants to work as a software engineer rather than in research...
heuristics.action: Enter industry directly rather than spending 4-5 years on a funded PhD stipend
heuristics.because: Multiple comments (534, 300 upvotes) note that the PhD premium is real for research roles but barely exists for SWE roles, and the opportunity cost of $32K/year vs $150K+ industry SWE salary rarely favors the PhD path

heuristics.rule: Be upfront about sponsorship needs during job search
heuristics.condition: When on STEM OPT and actively job searching for H-1B sponsorship...
