decision_factors.factor: CRS Score — raw competitive position
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a candidate will receive an ITA in general or category-based draws; candidates below cutoff thresholds are not selected
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Without PNP: need typically 500+ for general draws; 470–510 for STEM category draws (2025 benchmarks). With PNP: +600 makes virtually any score competitive

decision_factors.factor: Nationality relative to EB backlog
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Indian nationals represent 72.3% of H-1B approvals but face the same per-country ~7% EB visa quota as all other countries, creating a mathematically extreme backlog estimated at approximately 175 years at current rates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify worker's country of birth (not citizenship); Indian nationals face ~525,000+ pending petitions with only ~2,800–3,200 EB visas allocated to India per year; Chinese nationals face a qualitatively different 5–10 year EB-2 wait

decision_factors.factor: Age
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Age is a core human capital factor in CRS scoring; declining points after peak age window significantly reduces competitiveness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: CRS awards peak score for candidates aged 20–29; points decline significantly after age 45. Time-sensitive — delay in applying costs CRS points

decision_factors.factor: DOL Wage Level classification (I–IV)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Under the wage-weighted lottery effective February 27, 2026, wage level directly determines number of lottery entries (Level IV = 4 entries; Level I = 1 entry), affecting probability of cap selection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine the prevailing wage level assigned by the employer on the Labor Condition Application (LCA); current FY2023 distribution: Level I 10%, Level II 36%, Level III 35%, Level IV 19%

decision_factors.factor: Canadian work experience duration
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each year of Canadian work experience (up to 5 years) adds significant CRS points under core human capital and skill transferability factors
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current years of Canadian work experience; each additional year adds points up to the 5-year maximum

decision_factors.factor: Employer type: IT services firm vs. direct-hire tech company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: IT services firms (Cognizant, TCS, Infosys, Wipro) dominate absolute approval counts but at significantly lower wages than direct-hire tech companies (Amazon, Google, Microsoft), affecting both wage level classification and lottery advantage under new rules
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare employer category and offered wage against FY2023 medians: all H-1B $108,000; Computer occupations $124,000; Computer and Information Systems Managers $155,700

decision_factors.factor: NOC code classification
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for category-based STEM draws, PNP Tech streams, and the point value of a job offer (TEER 0/1 vs. other)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether occupation falls under targeted NOC codes (e.g., NOC 20012, NOC 21231, NOC 21232) for STEM draws and BC PNP Tech stream eligibility

decision_factors.factor: I-140 approval status and priority date
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An approved I-140 with a queued priority date enables AC21 portability for job changes and preserves the priority date even through layoffs, substantially affecting job mobility and stay-or-return optionality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether I-140 is approved; confirm priority date is in queue (not yet current); confirm 180-day threshold has been met before changing employers

decision_factors.factor: Language scores (CLB level)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: English/French language scores affect core human capital points and skill transferability points; CLB 9+ across all 4 bands maximizes points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use IELTS/CELPIP for English; TEF/TCF for French. Assess whether current scores reach CLB 9+ threshold for maximum points in all four language bands

decision_factors.factor: Occupation SOC code and H-1B specialty occupation classification
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Occupation determines prevailing wage benchmark, applicable wage level, and eligibility for H-1B specialty occupation classification; product managers file under SOC 11-3021 or 11-2021 with a median H-1B wage of $155,700 for Computer and Information Systems Managers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the SOC code on the LCA; computer-related occupations (SOC 15-xxxx) represent 65.1% of FY2023 approvals; management roles use SOC 11-xxxx codes

decision_factors.factor: Provincial Nominee Program eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PNP nomination adds +600 CRS points, which is the single largest available point boost and effectively guarantees ITA selection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess eligibility for province-specific streams (e.g., BC PNP Tech for tech workers with BC job offer; OINP Human Capital Priorities for Ontario candidates)

decision_factors.factor: Registration-to-approval probability under current lottery
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The average annual H-1B approval rate relative to registrations is approximately 22–28%, meaning most registrations do not result in selection; this directly affects planning certainty for international workers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use the USCIS-reported approximate 22–28% approval rate as a baseline probability; note this varies by year and registration volume

decision_factors.factor: Education level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Education is a core CRS human capital factor; PhD scores highest, bachelor's is baseline, no degree incurs significant penalty
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess highest completed credential; PhD maximizes education points, bachelor's degree is baseline reference

decision_factors.factor: Spouse/partner factors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If applicable, spouse/partner attributes (language, education, Canadian work experience) can add up to 40 additional CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether spouse/partner has qualifying language scores, education credentials, or Canadian work experience to contribute additional points

decision_factors.factor: Sibling in Canada (citizen or PR)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Having a sibling who is a Canadian citizen or PR adds +15 CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether a sibling holds Canadian citizenship or PR status

decision_factors.factor: Study in Canada
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Completing post-secondary education in Canada adds +30 CRS points (doctorate) or +15 points (secondary and above)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether the candidate completed eligible study in Canada at the appropriate level

decision_factors.factor: Inadmissibility history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Criminal records or previous visa violations can significantly extend processing times beyond the 6-month service standard and may affect final decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review applicant's history for criminal record, immigration violations, or other inadmissibility triggers before submitting application

decision_factors.factor: Nationality — comparative immigration backlog context
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For Indian nationals, Canadian PR (~1–2 years) vs. US EB-2 (~134 years) represents a fundamentally different immigration security situation; for Chinese nationals, US EB-2 backlog is 5–10 years vs. Canadian PR ~1–2 years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current immigration status country, nationality-specific backlogs, and timeline to permanent status in each jurisdiction

decision_factors.factor: Green card pathway category
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The difference between EB-2/EB-3 and EB-1A/EB-5 for Indian nationals is the difference between a 100+ year wait and a 2–4 year path — it fundamentally changes whether staying in the US is viable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine current I-140 category; check whether extraordinary ability or investor criteria could be met; get a legal opinion on EB-1A eligibility

decision_factors.factor: Green card tenure at point of return
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether exit tax applies at all; crossing the 8-of-15-year threshold triggers covered expatriate analysis and potential taxation of unrealized gains on all worldwide assets
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count the number of calendar years in the last 15 in which you held green card status; if fewer than 8, exit tax risk is zero regardless of net worth

decision_factors.factor: RRSP balance and treaty withholding rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The applicable non-resident withholding rate on RRSP withdrawals determines whether leaving RRSP funds in Canada is efficient; India and China get no treaty reduction, meaning 25% is the permanent rate on every future withdrawal
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check your home country's tax treaty with Canada specifically for pension/RRSP withholding rates; calculate your total RRSP balance and model the after-tax value under 25% withholding versus alternatives

decision_factors.factor: Per-country backlog position (priority date)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Your priority date determines where you are in the queue; a 2012 priority date means 12+ years have passed and you still cannot file — this is the single most concrete measure of how trapped you are
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare your priority date against the current Visa Bulletin cut-off date for your category and country; calculate the gap in years

decision_factors.factor: Net worth relative to the $2M covered expatriate threshold
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even if the 8-year tenure test is met, exit tax only triggers if net worth exceeds $2M or average annual US tax liability exceeds $190K; most employed professionals are below both thresholds
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Add fair market value of all worldwide assets minus liabilities; include 401k, IRAs, US real estate, home-country investments, and unvested equity at estimated value

decision_factors.factor: Non-registered investment portfolio size and unrealized gains
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Departure tax (deemed disposition) is triggered on non-registered investments at the moment you leave; larger portfolios with larger unrealized gains create larger immediate tax bills
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate current fair market value minus adjusted cost base for all non-registered holdings; estimate the capital gains tax at 50% inclusion rate at your expected marginal rate in the departure year

decision_factors.factor: Nationality (India vs. China vs. all others)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Per-country caps create wildly unequal wait times despite identical legal treatment — an Indian national faces 134-year EB-2 backlog while most other nationalities face 1–5 years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Simply identify passport country; Indian and Chinese nationals require completely different analysis than all others

decision_factors.factor: Home country tax residency rules and grace periods
decision_factors.why_it_matters: India's RNOR status creates a 2-year window where foreign income is not taxed domestically; China has no equivalent, making double taxation risk materially higher for Chinese returnees
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine home country residency trigger (India: 182-day rule plus prior residency history; China: 183-day rule) and whether any transitional status exists

decision_factors.factor: Departure date timing within the calendar year
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Leaving mid-year reduces your Canadian income for that year, potentially lowering your marginal rate for both RRSP withdrawals and deemed disposition gains — creating a planning window
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Project total Canadian income from January to departure date; model RRSP withdrawal scenarios at that lower income level versus the flat 25% non-resident rate post-departure

decision_factors.factor: Family size and dependent visa status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each dependent consumes one visa slot from the same per-country annual quota — a family of 4 uses 4 slots, effectively quadrupling the personal cost of the backlog
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count total family members who would need to be included in the green card application; multiply by the annual visa slot cost

decision_factors.factor: Existence and terms of applicable US tax treaty
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Tax treaties govern withholding rates on retirement distributions and can reduce the effective US tax burden on 401k/IRA withdrawals from 30% to 15% or zero
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the specific treaty article covering retirement income (e.g., US-India Article 20); confirm with custodian whether they honor treaty claims and what documentation is required

decision_factors.factor: Canadian real estate ownership and intended sale timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Selling Canadian real estate as a non-resident triggers Section 116 withholding at 25% of gross sale price — creating a major cash flow problem even when actual tax owed is far less
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether you plan to sell within a few years of departure; if yes, compare the net proceeds and process complexity of selling before versus after becoming a non-resident

decision_factors.factor: H-4 EAD dependency for spouse
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A spouse's ability to work in the US legally depends on the principal's I-140 approval and H-1B stage — if the principal loses their job, the spouse's work authorization is also at risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether spouse holds H-4 EAD; assess whether principal's I-140 is approved; model the household income risk if principal is laid off

decision_factors.factor: US real estate holdings at time of departure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Owning US property as a non-resident triggers FIRPTA withholding (15% of gross proceeds) on future sale; selling before departure avoids this entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify all US real property interests; evaluate whether selling before departure is financially viable given market conditions and timeline

decision_factors.factor: Strength of Canadian residential ties being severed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you fail to sever primary ties (home, spouse, dependents in Canada), CRA may continue to treat you as a Canadian tax resident even while you live abroad, resulting in ongoing worldwide taxation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit all primary and secondary residential ties using CRA's framework; document evidence of tie severance (lease termination, spouse relocation, cancellation of provincial health card, driver's license, etc.)

decision_factors.factor: Job change flexibility under H-1B
decision_factors.why_it_matters: H-1B holders cannot freely change employers without restarting certain processes; AC21 portability helps but has conditions — this creates career ceiling effects independent of skill
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether AC21 conditions are met (I-140 approved 180+ days, same or similar occupation); evaluate how many career moves have been foregone due to visa constraints

decision_factors.factor: Prior FBAR compliance history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Penalties for non-willful FBAR violations run up to $10,000/year and willful violations up to 50% of account balance per year; IRS enforces for prior years, not just current
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review whether FBARs were filed for each year foreign accounts exceeded $10,000 in aggregate while you were a US person; identify any gap years requiring voluntary disclosure

decision_factors.factor: HBP or LLP repayment obligations
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you withdrew from RRSP under the Home Buyers' Plan or Lifelong Learning Plan, the repayment obligation continues post-departure; failure to repay adds the required repayment amount to your income each year
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check your CRA My Account for outstanding HBP/LLP repayment balances and annual repayment schedule; calculate the cost of not repaying versus repaying before departure

decision_factors.factor: Legislative risk and policy change probability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Visa recapture acts or country-neutral allocation could dramatically accelerate priority dates — but Congress has repeatedly debated and not enacted these; basing a life plan on legislative hope is high-risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track active legislation; assess historical passage rate of similar bills; treat legislative relief as a low-probability upside, not a planning assumption

decision_factors.factor: Age and proximity to 401k distribution eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Early withdrawal before age 59½ triggers a 10% penalty plus ordinary income tax, making it almost always the worst financial option; age determines which distribution strategy is available
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate years until age 59½ and age 73 (RMD trigger under SECURE 2.0); model after-tax value of leaving funds to grow vs. early withdrawal under penalty

decision_factors.factor: CPP contribution history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: CPP entitlements are preserved after leaving Canada and represent a future income stream from your Canadian working years; they should factor into retirement income planning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review CPP Statement of Contributions through Service Canada; estimate projected CPP pension at age 65 based on years and amounts contributed

decision_factors.factor: Extraordinary ability eligibility (EB-1A criteria)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: EB-1A bypasses the entire per-country backlog with no employer sponsorship required — it is the primary escape hatch from the EB-2/EB-3 trap for Indian nationals
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate against USCIS criteria: publications, citations, awards, media coverage, salary relative to peers, judging others' work, memberships in distinguished associations

decision_factors.factor: Capital availability for EB-5
decision_factors.why_it_matters: EB-5 requires $800K–$1.05M investment but currently has no India backlog — for high-earning Indian professionals with savings or family capital, this may be the fastest permanent residency path
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess liquid or accessible capital; evaluate risk tolerance for investment; compare EB-5 processing timeline (4–12 months for rural/TEA) against career and family timeline

decision_factors.factor: Annual fiscal year visa exhaustion timing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even approved petitions go unfilled when annual caps are hit — EB-3/EW visas for FY2025 were exhausted by September 9, meaning the practical wait is longer than the queue position alone suggests
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Monitor USCIS Visa Bulletin monthly; track when prior fiscal years exhausted EB-3/EW supply; factor in that exhaustion is recurring, not exceptional

decision_factors.factor: Immigration status and PR security
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The entire stay-or-return calculus changes depending on whether the person has secured Canadian PR or is still on PGWP — PR eliminates visa precarity as a forcing function
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine current status (PGWP, PR application in process, PR confirmed, citizenship) and calculate 730-day compliance in the current 5-year window

decision_factors.factor: Household income structure (single vs. dual earner)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A single-income family and a dual-income family at the same gross household income have radically different savings trajectories because of how Canadian taxes, housing, and childcare costs interact
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Run the savings model explicitly for current household structure; then model what dual income would yield — the delta determines whether staying is financially defensible

decision_factors.factor: Age of children at time of return
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines severity of educational and identity disruption; different age windows carry categorically different risk profiles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the child's current age against the risk windows: under 5 (low risk), 5–15 (high risk), late high school or older (low risk)

decision_factors.factor: Partner's career viability in destination country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Return economics must work for both partners independently — a strong return case for one earner is invalidated if the other faces career relinquishment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the partner's field against job market depth in the target city; assess credential transferability; estimate realistic job search duration and income gap

decision_factors.factor: Parent's current age and health status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Age and health determine the realistic timeline and intensity of care needs, which changes whether return is urgent, plannable, or deferrable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map parent's current age to a rough care timeline: 60–65 typically means 5–10 years of independence remaining; 70–75 means 3–7 years; 75+ means care needs are already increasing with high variability

decision_factors.factor: Reverse culture shock probability and severity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High reverse culture shock risk can make an objectively good return decision feel like a mistake, leading to premature re-emigration and compounded disruption
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review how week 3 of your last extended home visit felt; assess how different your values, communication norms, and daily preferences are from home-country norms; evaluate whether you identify as a Third Culture Individual

decision_factors.factor: Net annual savings rate (PPP-adjusted)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: This is the actual unit of wealth accumulation; gross salary comparisons are misleading and this is the corrected metric
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Run the full deduction template for both scenarios, convert home-country savings using PPP factors for local goods only, and compare as a percentage of gross

decision_factors.factor: Sector-specific returnee premium
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US experience commands a strong premium in some sectors (Tech, PE/VC, Academia in China) and near-zero premium in others (state banking, government civil service) — this directly determines compensation and career trajectory upon return
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether companies in your specific sector actively recruit US-experienced candidates; check if talent programs or headhunters in your field specifically target US returnees; look at leadership profiles at target employers

decision_factors.factor: Liquid savings threshold (separate from retirement accounts)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines financial resilience during the transition — covers career gap, return costs, housing downpayment, and time to find the right role without desperation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Classify yourself by risk profile: conservative ($300K–$500K), moderate ($150K–$250K), aggressive ($80K–$120K); aggressive only valid if family housing available, no children, partner already employed in home country, and specific offer in hand

decision_factors.factor: Career ceiling by market for your specific role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The ceiling varies dramatically by field and background; staying may be optimal in some niches (certain AI research, biotech) and suboptimal in others where home-market demand is surging
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the most senior roles achievable in your specific function in each market; assess whether a foreign-background professional has reached those roles; check glass ceiling effects for your demographic in the host country

decision_factors.factor: Savings rate over 10-year horizon
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines actual net worth accumulation, which is the real output of career decisions — not gross salary
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model monthly take-home after taxes and fixed costs (rent, healthcare, transportation) for each path, project savings monthly, and compound over 10 years

decision_factors.factor: Immigration pathway realism
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The visa or green card path you are counting on may be structurally unavailable within your planning horizon, making your entire career plan contingent on an event that won't occur
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up current priority dates for your specific category and country of birth; for Indian EB-2/EB-3, calculate realistic wait time based on current movement rates, not optimistic estimates

decision_factors.factor: Savings rate differential (CAD vs. home country PPP)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian net savings for a typical Toronto tech professional (~$18,000–$20,000 CAD/year) are low enough that home-country purchasing power may be comparable, weakening the financial case for staying
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate monthly net savings in CAD after Toronto expenses; convert to USD; then model equivalent savings in home city using PPP-adjusted cost of living

decision_factors.factor: City-level housing cost
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Housing is the single largest variable in Canadian savings arithmetic — it can mean the difference between $546/month saved and $3,447/month saved at comparable income levels
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use current or anticipated rent as a fixed monthly cost; compare Toronto core vs. suburbs vs. mid-cost Canadian cities (Edmonton, Calgary, Saskatoon) to quantify the savings delta

decision_factors.factor: Child's primary language of thought and social identity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A child who primarily thinks and dreams in English will struggle to adapt to a Mandarin or Hindi-medium school environment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask what language the child primarily uses at home, with friends, and when thinking internally; assess years spent in US school system

decision_factors.factor: Partner's immigration status in the destination country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A foreign-born partner relocating to the primary earner's home country may face restricted work authorization that is not solved by spousal visa alone
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the destination country (China, India) grants work authorization to foreign spouses automatically or requires separate employer sponsorship; compare against third-country options

decision_factors.factor: Sibling presence and care-sharing capacity in home country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The presence of siblings who can share physical caregiving directly determines whether your return is structurally necessary or whether alternatives exist
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether siblings are geographically close to parents, willing and able to coordinate care, and whether care responsibility can be split between local presence and your financial support from abroad

decision_factors.factor: Quality and vitality of home-country social network
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Social isolation is a primary driver of failed repatriation; returning without live relationships accelerates identity confusion and belonging-nowhere syndrome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether close friendships back home still feel alive despite years apart; determine whether friends who stayed have diverged significantly in worldview and shared reference points

decision_factors.factor: State income tax in US location
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Ranges from 0% to 13.3%, creating up to a $20K+ annual difference for the same job depending on state — this alone can swing the savings rate comparison
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the specific state; apply the correct marginal and effective rate to the gross salary in the model

decision_factors.factor: License portability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For medicine and law, credentials earned in the US do not automatically qualify practice in China or India — re-licensing may require passing exams in a different language on a different legal/medical system, which is a hard structural barrier
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the exact re-qualification pathway for your profession in your target country; estimate time and cost; determine whether the path is realistically completable given your current language proficiency and time since training

decision_factors.factor: Home-country network density and quality
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines speed and quality of role acquisition on return — the difference between 1–3 months and 6–18 months of job search, and whether you return to a role or return to frustration
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count the number of specific individuals in your target home city who know your work quality and can hire or refer you; target minimum of 3–5 such relationships built before departure

decision_factors.factor: Immigration tax — true cost of maintaining status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Visa constraints foreclose opportunities available to domestic peers: starting a company, switching employers freely, taking career risks; these costs are rarely quantified but compound over years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate annual legal fees, estimate mental overhead and time cost, list specific opportunities you have declined or cannot pursue due to visa status, estimate probability-weighted timeline to permanent status

decision_factors.factor: Immigration tax — financial, time, and opportunity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Significantly reduces the real value of US compensation and restricts career mobility in ways that compound over time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate annual legal fees ($3k–$8k), total green card process costs ($20k–$100k), hours per year spent on immigration overhead, and enumerate specific career actions you cannot take on H-1B

decision_factors.factor: Sector-specific opportunity gap between host and home country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The gap between what's possible at home vs. in the US has narrowed in specific sectors (AI, EV, biotech, fintech in China; VC-backed tech in India) but has NOT narrowed equally across all sectors
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your specific sector and map where the frontier work, funding, and talent concentration actually sits — do not assume the answer is the same across fields

decision_factors.factor: Partner's work authorization and career mobility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada allows partners to work freely on open work permits; the US does not for H-4 dependents (with limited exceptions) — this asymmetry materially affects household income and partner satisfaction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine partner's current visa status in Canada and whether they are employed; model what happens to their employment status in each scenario (stay, move to US, return home)

decision_factors.factor: CWELCC childcare subsidy eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Subsidized childcare at ~$10/day vs. unsubsidized daycare represents a $12,000–$21,600/year difference in annual savings — material enough to shift the stay-vs-return calculation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether the province has implemented CWELCC and whether the family qualifies; model both the subsidized and unsubsidized scenarios for the specific province

decision_factors.factor: All-in cost of schooling in destination city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: International school fees ($15,000–$50,000/year per child) can significantly erode the financial upside of returning, especially if multiple children are involved
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research specific international school fees in the target city; multiply by number of children and years until university; subtract from projected savings-rate improvement

decision_factors.factor: Dual-earner vs. single-earner household structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Dual-earner couples are materially less geographically mobile than single-earner couples because relocation requires both partners to find acceptable outcomes simultaneously
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether both partners are actively building careers or one is not currently working; if dual-earner, require independent career analysis for both before deciding

decision_factors.factor: Elder care infrastructure quality in the home city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Where professional care infrastructure exists and is affordable, remote management of care becomes viable; where it doesn't, physical presence becomes harder to substitute
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research availability of professional caregivers, elder care facilities, and care coordination services in the parent's specific city; tier-1 cities in China and India have increasingly viable options, rural areas much less so

decision_factors.factor: Availability of returnee communities in target city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Communities of other returnees provide a social context where the dual-identity experience is understood, significantly accelerating re-adaptation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether major cities in the home country (Shanghai, Beijing, Mumbai, Bangalore) have active returnee professional communities; assess accessibility of those networks

decision_factors.factor: Housing cost in specific city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Rent in major US tech hubs runs $30K–$66K/year and is the single largest post-tax expenditure, often exceeding the tax burden
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use current market rent for a realistic unit size (not minimum) in the actual city of employment, not national averages

decision_factors.factor: Income compression magnitude by sector
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The compression ranges from moderate (Tech: 30–50%) to severe (Medicine: 70–85%); this determines whether the return is financially viable and changes the entire savings/wealth-building calculus
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Benchmark current US total comp against realistic total comp at equivalent-level roles in target country; convert to PPP-adjusted terms; calculate net savings rate in each scenario rather than comparing gross figures

decision_factors.factor: Title and scope level at time of return
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines the quality of roles available in the home country and your credibility as a returnee — home-country employers benchmark against US credentials
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For tech: Senior/Staff or above (L5/L6 equivalent); for finance: VP or MD level; for academia: PhD plus postdoc with publications; assess whether current trajectory reaches target within 3–7 years

decision_factors.factor: Savings rate differential (not gross salary)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Net wealth accumulation is what compounds; gross salary comparisons without adjusting for taxes, cost of living, remittances, and purchasing power systematically mislead the analysis
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Build a simple model: gross income minus taxes, rent, living costs, legal fees, remittances; compare residual savings and their purchasing power in each market

decision_factors.factor: Career ceiling in each market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines the maximum compensation and leadership trajectory available, which drives 10–20 year wealth and impact outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether C-suite and VP roles are realistically accessible given language, cultural, and visa constraints in the US; assess whether returnee premium and lower leadership competition create a higher ceiling at home

decision_factors.factor: Entrepreneurship intent
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If founding a company is part of your plan, the US visa system imposes structural barriers that don't exist at home, making return or third-country options disproportionately attractive
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether you would pursue entrepreneurship within 5 years; if yes, map the legal pathway available to you on your current visa status and compare it to the frictionless path at home

decision_factors.factor: Canadian passport value relative to home country passport
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For Indian and Chinese nationals, Canadian citizenship represents a significant upgrade in global visa-free access (185+ countries vs. significantly fewer for Indian/Chinese passports)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare visa-free country count between current passport and Canadian passport; assess how frequently the individual travels internationally for work or personal reasons

decision_factors.factor: Immigration security (Canadian PR status)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PR eliminates immigration uncertainty, job lock, visa renewal costs, and H-1B lottery anxiety — a psychological and financial benefit the savings model does not capture but that some professionals rationally price highly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether PR has been obtained or is on a clear pathway; without it, the savings model understates the true cost of staying in Canada

decision_factors.factor: Citizenship and legal identity of children in home country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: China does not recognize dual citizenship; India prohibits it — these legal realities determine school access, university admission tracks, and future identity choices
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine the child's legal status in the destination country (foreign national, OCI holder, treated as domestic national) and map the practical consequences for schooling and travel

decision_factors.factor: Who is driving the decision vs. who is trailing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The trailing partner absorbs disproportionate career and network disruption; if the decision is perceived as one person's sacrifice, resentment risk is high
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask each partner separately what they want in their own terms; assess whether the non-driving partner has a real career path or is being asked to start from scratch

decision_factors.factor: What type of support the parent actually needs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Financial support and medical decision-making can be provided remotely; daily logistics and emotional presence require physical proximity — the specific care need determines whether return is necessary
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Break down support needed into: financial (sendable from anywhere), emotional presence (requires proximity or very frequent visits), medical decisions (manageable remotely except in crises), daily logistics (requires local presence or a coordinator)

decision_factors.factor: Whether the return role leverages international experience as advantage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Roles that treat US experience as a competitive asset validate the returnee's identity and reduce belonging-nowhere friction; roles that ignore or penalize it worsen repatriation distress
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether the prospective employer or role specifically values US-market exposure, cross-cultural fluency, or international network; determine if the role allows you to operate differently from local peers

decision_factors.factor: Children and education costs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Childcare in US cities adds $18K–$42K/year per child; international school in China adds ¥200K–¥350K/year — these costs can eliminate savings entirely in either scenario
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine number of children, ages, and schooling needs; apply city-specific childcare or international school cost to the relevant scenario

decision_factors.factor: Political and regulatory risk in target sector
decision_factors.why_it_matters: China's regulatory environment has become more restrictive since 2021 — finance and tech sectors have faced crackdowns; this creates career and income volatility that is not captured in a point-in-time salary comparison
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track sector-specific regulatory history in target country over the past 3–5 years; assess whether your target sector has been subject to government restrictions; evaluate downside scenarios if regulatory crackdown hits your employer

decision_factors.factor: Specific role or founding plan identified before departure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The presence or absence of a specific role before leaving is the single biggest determinant of transition success — it eliminates the weak-position job search scenario
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is there a concrete offer letter, a founding plan with committed LPs, or a named professorship offer? If not, the return trigger has not been met regardless of other milestones

decision_factors.factor: Equity and ownership access
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Wage income has a ceiling; equity in startups, property ownership, and business stakes are the primary wealth-compounding mechanisms and differ sharply between markets and visa statuses
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your visa status allows you to found or co-found a company; evaluate property ownership rights; compare startup ecosystem quality and access to founding opportunities in each market

decision_factors.factor: Visa status and employer dependency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employer knowledge of high switching costs for visa holders depresses wage growth and stunts career mobility for years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether you are on H-1B, how many years to green card, and whether your employer knows your switching costs are high; research finding: 50% of visa-holding researchers felt trapped, 80% reported restricted job prospects

decision_factors.factor: Compensation differential adjusted for life goals
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US top-end compensation ($350K-$1M+ at senior levels) is genuinely exceptional and not yet replicated in most home markets — but this advantage only materializes for top performers at elite companies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether you are realistically on a path to senior/principal roles at top-tier companies, not median-case; also assess whether financial maximization or optionality/entrepreneurship is your primary goal

decision_factors.factor: Aging parent proximity and care obligations
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada does not solve geographic distance from aging parents; if care needs are real and immediate, financial and immigration advantages do not offset the proximity problem
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess parents' current health status, whether siblings or other family can provide care, and whether the care need is imminent or speculative

decision_factors.factor: Home-country city tier and earning potential
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The break-even calculation depends on which home-country city is the comparison — a Bangalore/Hyderabad senior tech professional compresses the Canada advantage significantly more than a Tier 2 city comparison
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model the specific home-country scenario: gross income at realistic senior title, take-home after local taxes, expenses in the relevant city, and resulting annual savings in PPP-adjusted USD

decision_factors.factor: Reversibility of the decision if children do not adapt
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A return that doesn't work for the children creates a painful secondary decision under worse conditions; families without a contingency plan get trapped
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: if children are unhappy after 2 years, what is the plan? Does the family retain visa status, job options, or housing in the US?

decision_factors.factor: Financial cost and duration of transition income gap
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The trailing partner typically faces 3–12 months of income loss during job search; split-family arrangements add $5,000–$10,000/month in dual household costs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model combined household income during the transition period; identify who absorbs the shortfall and for how long the plan remains financially viable

decision_factors.factor: Parents' own stated preferences regarding your return
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Many return decisions are driven by the professional's peace of mind rather than the parent's actual needs or wishes; the parent's preference is a key variable that is rarely explicitly surfaced
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have a direct conversation with parents about whether they want you to return or prefer you remain abroad and succeed; ask specifically if they would rather have your career success and professional care funding versus your physical presence

decision_factors.factor: Country-specific environmental stressors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Infrastructure friction, censorship, bureaucracy, pollution, and social pressure norms create persistent low-grade stress that compounds identity disorientation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For China: assess comfort with WeChat-only ecosystem, hierarchy norms, political environment. For India: assess tolerance for bureaucratic friction, pollution levels in target city, family pressure dynamics around marriage and living arrangements

decision_factors.factor: Currency risk on home-country savings
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RMB and INR have experienced significant depreciation vs. USD in certain periods; savings in local currency may lose real value relative to USD-denominated wealth
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review 10-year historical exchange rate trajectory for the home currency; assess whether savings will remain in local currency or be converted

decision_factors.factor: Career ceiling at VP/CXO level by sector and country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some sectors (Tech in China, PE/VC) allow returnees to reach senior leadership; others (state banks, government) structurally exclude returnees from top roles — this determines long-term career trajectory, not just entry-level compensation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research the leadership profiles of senior executives (VP and above) at target employer types; determine what fraction are returnees vs. domestic-track; look for patterns in who gets promoted to C-suite

decision_factors.factor: Partner/spouse career alignment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Dual-income families and those with partners who have independent career trajectories have different financial thresholds and must have both careers mapped before departure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the partner identified specific home-country career paths? Are both people's professional networks and role pipelines ready simultaneously? Misalignment here can cause one partner to sacrifice career continuity

decision_factors.factor: Realistic probability-weighted timeline to permanent residence
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The expected value of staying changes radically depending on whether permanent status is 3 years away or 25 years away or functionally impossible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your specific visa category and backlog; calculate realistic median time to permanent status; assign probability that the path completes given policy risk; multiply by the value of the rights it unlocks

decision_factors.factor: Family and inherited wealth assets in home country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Property, business assets, and family wealth create wealth floors unavailable abroad that dramatically alter the financial comparison
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Explicitly value family property, business interests, or inheritance expectations in the home country and include them in net worth projections

decision_factors.factor: Peer comparison set shift
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The social proof and peer pressure to stay that operated for earlier cohorts is weakening; 'most people from my school are staying' is less true now, changing what counts as a conventional vs. contrarian choice
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look at recent cohort data from your specific school and field, not anecdotal impressions from older graduates

decision_factors.factor: Canada-US salary differential for the specific role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The 3–5× annual savings gap between comparable Canadian and US tech roles is large enough to materially affect long-term wealth compounding; staying in Canada vs. moving to the US is not financially neutral
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare total compensation for the specific role in Canadian city vs. comparable US city (e.g., Toronto SWE vs. Seattle SWE); model after-tax savings over 5 and 10 years

decision_factors.factor: Provincial tax jurisdiction
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Province of residence creates a $3,000–$8,000/year difference in after-tax income at comparable gross incomes — BC and Ontario are higher-tax environments than Alberta
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare provincial tax rates for the relevant income bracket; factor into take-home calculations before comparing to home-country savings

decision_factors.factor: University admission pathway for children
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OCI and foreign-passport-holding children in India and China are placed on separate, typically less favorable admission tracks for elite universities
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether the child would enter domestic or NRI/overseas quota tracks at target universities; compare seat availability and fee structures

decision_factors.factor: Availability of viable destination cities for both career fields simultaneously
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Return city options are constrained by what job markets exist for both fields — some combinations (tech + finance) are viable in major hubs; others (tech + academia) may not be
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map both careers' required city footprint against available destination cities; check whether any single city satisfies both

decision_factors.factor: Career stage and mobility at the time eldercare pressure peaks
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Eldercare pressure structurally peaks during the 30s–40s, which is also the peak career opportunity and mobility window; the cost of returning early is highest at exactly this moment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate the lifetime earnings differential between remaining on the US trajectory versus returning at the current career stage; for senior tech professionals this can be $500,000–$2,000,000 over 20 years

decision_factors.factor: Realistic expectations calibration before departure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Both idealizing and dreading the return predict worse outcomes; calibrated, realistic expectations are the single most consistent predictor of successful repatriation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit whether your mental image of home is based on current reality or a decade-old memory; identify specific things you assume will be true that may have changed

decision_factors.factor: Immigration legal costs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: H-1B and green card legal fees of $5K–$15K/year reduce US net savings materially and represent a cost with no equivalent in the home-country scenario
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine current visa stage and expected timeline to green card; annualize total projected legal and filing costs over that period

decision_factors.factor: Research infrastructure quality in academia
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For academic returnees, the quality of lab infrastructure, funding availability, and institutional reputation determines whether they can maintain international research competitiveness — a weak institution can stall a research career regardless of the recruitment package
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate Nature/Science publication rates at target institution; assess startup fund adequacy for your specific research area; check whether returnees at that institution have maintained international collaboration and publication rates post-return

decision_factors.factor: Unvested equity schedule
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Represents a concrete, time-sensitive financial asset that is forfeited if departure timing is not planned around vesting events
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Pull the vesting schedule and calculate the dollar value of unvested equity at various departure dates; factor this into negotiating home-country start dates

decision_factors.factor: Family financial assets and obligations in home market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Inheritance, family business, property, and aging parent care are asymmetric: they only compound at home and cannot be captured remotely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate value of home-country family assets you stand to be involved with; assess aging parents' care timeline; evaluate whether a family business requires your physical presence to grow or preserve value

decision_factors.factor: Currency appreciation risk
decision_factors.why_it_matters: USD has historically appreciated vs. RMB and INR, which changes long-term wealth calculations if savings are held in or converted to home currency
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model scenarios where USD strengthens 10–30% vs. home currency over 10 years and assess how that changes relative wealth accumulation

decision_factors.factor: Psychological cost of permanent temporariness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Being indefinitely on a work visa has documented psychological costs — feeling trapped, restricted career mobility, status tracking, missed family milestones — that do not appear in salary comparisons
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Among H-1B holders surveyed, 50% felt trapped and 80% felt their career was meaningfully restricted; honestly assess whether you are already experiencing these symptoms

decision_factors.factor: Children's schooling and settlement depth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Once children are enrolled in Canadian schools and have formed local social connections, return disruption costs rise significantly and become a real constraint on the decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess children's ages, years in Canadian school system, and language/social integration level; younger children have lower disruption costs than teenagers

decision_factors.factor: CAD/USD exchange rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian salaries are 25–40% lower than USD equivalents for the same role, and savings expressed in CAD need to be converted at ~0.73 to compare against USD-denominated home-country comparisons
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Convert Canadian savings to USD equivalent using current CAD/USD rate; use PPP conversion for home-country comparisons rather than market exchange rates

decision_factors.factor: Child's expressed preferences
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Older children who have formed social and educational identity in the US may resist relocation, creating family conflict that undermines the return
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Directly ask children old enough to have a view; weight their input more heavily as they approach adolescence

decision_factors.factor: Relationship quality risk from split-family arrangements
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Split-family arrangements sustained beyond 6 months are associated with significant relationship quality decline per research
decision_factors.how_to_assess: If a split-family phase is unavoidable, define its maximum duration explicitly and build a hard decision point at the 6-month mark

decision_factors.factor: Partner and family alignment on eldercare response
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A return decision driven by one partner's eldercare obligation affects the entire household; without partner alignment, the decision creates compounding personal and relationship costs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess explicitly whether partner is onboard with return, understands the drivers, and has a viable path in the home country

decision_factors.factor: Timeline patience and financial runway
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Research suggests stabilization takes 12–24 months; people who lack financial runway or patience to wait through peak distress at months 6–12 make premature re-emigration decisions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether you have financial and professional stability to absorb 12–24 months of adjustment difficulty without needing to make a second major move

decision_factors.factor: Job mobility constraints under H-1B
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The inability to freely switch employers without visa risk limits career optionality and may suppress compensation growth relative to what a free agent could achieve
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how close you are to green card; determine whether your employer and role constrain your ability to pursue better offers

decision_factors.factor: Private vs. state sector distinction within country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Within the same country, private-sector and state-sector roles have fundamentally different dynamics for returnees — the returnee premium, promotion ceiling, and regulatory exposure differ dramatically
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Classify each specific opportunity as private-market, state-owned enterprise, or government; apply the appropriate ceiling and premium assessment for each category rather than treating the country as uniform

decision_factors.factor: Home-country licensing or credential portability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In fields like medicine, US credentials do not automatically transfer — clinical licensing in the home country may take 2–3 additional years, fundamentally changing the return timeline and viable return paths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research the specific licensing pathway in your field in your target country; determine whether clinical, research, industry, or administrative tracks are viable and on what timeline

decision_factors.factor: Partner's career and immigration status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner whose visa is dependent on yours, or whose career is tied to the host country, changes the payoff matrix for both people
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your partner's ideal scenario explicitly; assess what each path costs them professionally and personally; determine whether their career compounds more in host country or home country

decision_factors.factor: Entrepreneurship accessibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Home country allows free pivoting, company founding, and independent consulting without visa authorization; US H-1B actively restricts these
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether you can start a company, take a gap, switch industries, or consult independently in each location without immigration consequences

decision_factors.factor: Research and innovation frontier access
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For specific research roles (advanced AI, certain biotech), the US still concentrates global talent, compute, and funding in ways that are not yet replicable at home
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether your specific research area requires access to infrastructure, collaborators, or publication networks that are genuinely US-concentrated, versus fields where this is no longer true

decision_factors.factor: Concreteness of home-country opportunity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Returning to a vague 'idea' of home-country opportunity versus a specific job offer or business plan has dramatically different risk profiles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the person has a specific offer, a business plan with identified customers/funding, or is returning to 'figure it out' — only the first two justify treating it as a concrete opportunity

decision_factors.factor: Universal healthcare (no premium deductions)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unlike the US model, Canadian take-home is not reduced by employer health insurance premiums — this improves net income relative to a US comparison but is often not factored in when professionals compare Canada to the US
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note that Canadian tax models do not require a separate health insurance line item; the comparison to US-based models must adjust for this structural difference

decision_factors.factor: Bilingual education access in destination city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Children raised with strong English plus home-country language have global optionality; this outcome depends on the quality of international or bilingual schools available
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify specific bilingual or international schools in the target city; assess whether they deliver genuine bilingual outcomes or are primarily one-language with the other as an add-on

decision_factors.factor: Gender asymmetry in trailing partner burden
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Women are significantly more likely to be the trailing partner in international relocation decisions and face larger career interruptions — this skews who bears the cost of the decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify which partner is more likely to be trailing and whether that distribution is equitable and explicitly agreed upon

decision_factors.factor: Cost of professional care relative to US income
decision_factors.why_it_matters: On a US salary, high-quality professional elder care in China or India is often affordable, which changes the framing of whether physical return is the only way to fulfill care obligations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare actual cost of professional care (¥10,000–¥30,000/month in China tier-1; ₹15,000–₹40,000/month in India) against the career and earnings cost of returning; assess whether funded professional care is a genuine substitute for the specific care need

decision_factors.factor: Home-country investment return environment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Local stock market and real estate returns determine whether home-country savings compound effectively; Chinese real estate has been in a downturn 2023–2025
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research current and historical returns for home-country equity and real estate markets; compare to US equity market baseline

decision_factors.factor: Whether the urgency is family-driven versus financially optimal
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Family-driven urgency (eldercare crisis, partner preference) is a legitimate override of financial milestones; absence of family urgency means financial thresholds should be honored before returning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Explicitly identify whether the pressure to return comes from a concrete family need or from generalized emotional pull; if the latter, assess whether milestones are actually met

decision_factors.factor: Home-market demand for your specific skills
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Not all fields have equal home-market demand; AI, biotech, and finance in Shanghai or Mumbai may rival or exceed opportunities abroad, but this is field- and city-specific
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research compensation and role availability for your specific function in target home-market cities; talk to practitioners working in that market; assess trajectory of the sector over next 5 years

decision_factors.factor: Home market startup and VC ecosystem maturity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A maturing home ecosystem means returnees can access growth opportunities, leadership roles, and equity that previously only existed in the US
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research home country VC investment rank, unicorn count, and sector competitiveness (China ranks 4th globally for VC; India 5th for unicorns); assess whether target sector is globally competitive at home

decision_factors.factor: Third-country viability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada, Singapore, UAE, and UK offer immigration stability and career quality combinations that may dominate both the US and home country for specific profiles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For Canada: assess Express Entry CRS score. For Singapore: assess EP eligibility. For UAE: model post-tax income given zero income tax. For UK: assess Global Talent Visa eligibility. Compare these concretely, not hypothetically.

decision_factors.factor: Universal healthcare and social safety net valuation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unlike US H-1B holders for whom employer-sponsored health insurance is a significant stay-anchor, Canadian PR holders already have universal healthcare — this is not a reason to stay in Canada vs. return home, but it is a reason Canada beats the US on security
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether the individual or family has ongoing healthcare needs that would be costly to manage privately; evaluate childcare costs under CWELCC subsidy vs. home country

decision_factors.factor: 10-year household trajectory
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Current savings rate is only one dimension — the more important question is what happens to this household's compounding over a decade, factoring in career growth, potential equity, and asset accumulation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the current savings differential is likely to widen or narrow over 10 years; assess whether the Canadian career has a visible trajectory toward significantly higher income

decision_factors.factor: One-time transition costs of returning
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Tax filing for departure year, cross-border CPA fees, income gap during job search, and relocation costs can total $20K–$50K+ in the return year
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Enumerate: departure-year tax filing cost, months of expected job search gap, relocation costs, and any covered expatriate tax exposure

decision_factors.factor: Advisory or consulting engagements with home-country companies while in the US
decision_factors.why_it_matters: These serve dual purpose: verifying that the home-country market is as expected, and building the network credentialing required for fast role acquisition on return
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have you completed 1–2 paid or advisory engagements with home-country companies? Have these relationships progressed to the point of hire-or-refer capability?

decision_factors.factor: Currency exposure over 10 years
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Currency appreciation or depreciation of home currency against dollar/CAD affects the real value of savings and transfers over a decade
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess expected trajectory of home currency; consider where you plan to spend savings long-term; evaluate whether dollar-denominated savings are actually more valuable given your end-use scenario

decision_factors.factor: Returnee premium (海归 effect)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: International exposure is scarce and valued at many home country companies, creating premium positioning unavailable to those who never left
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether target employers in the home country actively recruit returnees and whether international credentials command salary or role premiums

decision_factors.factor: Local Canadian network strength
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian career mobility and opportunity discovery depend heavily on local professional networks; someone without an established network has lower switching costs for leaving
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the person has Canadian professional references, a local peer group in their field, and has been promoted or changed jobs within Canada successfully

decision_factors.factor: US network maintenance cost if returning
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Preserving professional relationships in the US after return requires $5K–$15K/year in travel costs that reduce the financial benefit of returning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate number of trips per year needed to maintain relevant US professional relationships and price at current airfare

decision_factors.factor: Income compression severity by field
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The financial gap between US and home-country compensation varies enormously by field — for US-trained physicians it is so severe that many choose not to return to clinical practice at all
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research actual compensation data for equivalent roles in your target city; calculate the long-term compounding impact of the salary differential; distinguish between fields where gap closes (tech, finance) versus remains permanent (clinical medicine)

decision_factors.factor: Proximity to aging parents at critical years
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Parents' health crises and final years are not evenly distributed across time; missing them is irreversible and has psychological costs that don't appear in financial models
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess parents' current age and health trajectory; estimate when caregiving needs are likely to peak; evaluate whether remote support is genuinely adequate or a rationalization

decision_factors.factor: US education and immigration total investment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The $400k–$800k total investment must compound significantly to beat a career that started earlier at home — this threshold is often not modeled
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Sum 4-year education and living costs, immigration legal fees, and foregone earnings during study; then determine whether realistic career outcome exceeds this break-even

decision_factors.factor: Profile type (international student vs. experienced hire vs. US transit)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The three profiles (PGWP grad, Express Entry mid-career, US H-1B transit) have different risk exposures, financial baselines, and optionality sets — advice that is correct for one profile may be wrong for another
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify which profile the person belongs to; adjust the decision framework based on their age, career stage, immigration status, and original motivation for being in Canada

decision_factors.factor: Depth of social roots and whether they matter to your 10-year self
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Social roots compound slowly and are hard to rebuild; the value of deep roots depends on how much you weight community belonging versus mobility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask honestly whether you have built genuine deep relationships in the host country or are still primarily connected to an expat/international community; project which matters more to you at 40

decision_factors.factor: Whether the field is more meritocratic in host country or home country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In less meritocratic home markets, advancement depends on network and family connections that an internationally-educated returnee may or may not have
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether top performers in your field at home rose on credentials and output or on family/political connections; assess whether your specific network advantages are transferable

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency (TEF Canada B1)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unlocks Bilingual Advantage points — the highest single-variable CRS gain available to most candidates, worth up to ~50 points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate current French level; determine if B1 is achievable within 3-6 months given time and study resources available

decision_factors.factor: Country-of-birth backlog for US green card
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For nationals of India (and China), the EB-2/EB-3 priority date backlog makes US permanent residency functionally unavailable within a normal career horizon, fundamentally changing the risk calculus
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the USCIS Visa Bulletin for your preference category and country of birth; calculate realistic wait time in years, not months

decision_factors.factor: PGWP open permit awareness — job mobility rights
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PGWP holders can change employers freely, but many behave as if they are tied to a single employer, causing career paralysis and missed opportunities
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm work permit type: if PGWP (open work permit), employer changes are unrestricted — no LMIA required, no status risk from job change

decision_factors.factor: Program length and type (standard vs. co-op/joint)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PGWP duration is tied to program length with a 3-year maximum; co-op and integrated programs may have ambiguous length calculations that affect PGWP duration
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the completion letter specifies the full integrated program duration including co-op; confirm whether IRCC counts total enrollment months or academic-only months

decision_factors.factor: PGWP expiry date and remaining validity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employers may hesitate if PGWP expiry is imminent, as it shortens the practical employment window before PR is needed; being specific about the date demonstrates transparency and planning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: State the exact expiry date in your authorization disclosure; assess whether remaining validity covers a typical employment horizon employers care about

decision_factors.factor: PGWP duration relative to program length
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 3-year PGWP gives substantially more runway to accumulate CEC-eligible experience, job-search, and maximize CRS score versus a 1-year PGWP, which creates extreme time pressure on every step
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check your program length: programs of 2+ years yield the maximum 3-year PGWP; programs under 2 years yield a PGWP matching the program length, capped at 3 years

decision_factors.factor: Company size and sponsorship track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Big tech sponsors routinely; small startups and consulting firms often cannot or will not — this determines whether H-1B sponsorship is even a realistic outcome regardless of your qualifications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the recruiter directly; check LinkedIn for current employees with H-1B status; research company E-Verify enrollment for STEM OPT eligibility

decision_factors.factor: Visa disclosure timing in the outreach funnel
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Disclosing sponsorship needs too early in the outreach sequence allows HR filters or busy managers to reject before any relationship is established; disclosing after demonstrating value reverses the leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: has there been a two-way conversation where the other party has expressed genuine interest in you as a candidate? If yes, it is safe to surface visa status. If no, delay

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's industry network and internship pipeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether a PhD student gets internships at top AI labs and industry research roles; a rank-20 program advisor with Google Brain connections can outplace a rank-5 advisor with no industry ties
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor where their last 5 students interned; check LinkedIn for placement outcomes of former PhD students; ask which companies the advisor actively collaborates with

decision_factors.factor: Remaining OPT/STEM OPT time
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The amount of time left on OPT determines how much runway exists to find a new sponsor before status expires, directly constraining which options are viable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining on EAD card against the H-1B cap registration deadline (early March) and typical employer onboarding timelines

decision_factors.factor: I-20 program end date vs. OPT EAD expiration date
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The 60-day grace period trigger depends on which date controls your authorized stay — these two dates are not always the same and confusing them leads to overstay risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare your I-20 program end date against your OPT EAD expiration date; whichever ends first may determine when the grace period clock starts

decision_factors.factor: Long-term immigration intent
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students who plan to stay in the US long-term face compounding downstream risk from Day 1 CPT because USCIS scrutiny at H-1B and green card stages can resurface early CPT authorization questions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the student plans to apply for H-1B, green card, or other status extensions after graduation — if yes, risk profile is materially worse

decision_factors.factor: Employer size and H-1B sponsorship experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Small or inexperienced employers may not have the legal infrastructure or willingness to navigate H-1B specialty occupation documentation, increasing denial risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR directly; check USCIS H-1B employer data disclosures or DOL LCA database for prior filings

decision_factors.factor: Genuineness of cap-exempt employment relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: USCIS can audit the arrangement; if the cap-exempt employment is found to be nominal rather than real, the consequences are serious — including potential status violations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the individual will actually perform work for the cap-exempt entity, not just nominally hold a title; the part-time allocation (~20%) must correspond to real duties

decision_factors.factor: Company H-1B sponsorship history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A return offer from a company with no sponsorship history provides no path to legal work authorization after OPT expires — the internship conversion advantage is nullified
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up the company on H1Bdata.info or MyVisaJobs; flag any company with fewer than 5 H-1B filings per year as high risk

decision_factors.factor: Quality of Plan B (Canada or other country) as a genuine alternative
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether the backup option feels like a real choice vs. a consolation prize directly affects psychological resilience during the uncertainty window and the quality of the final decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have you actively researched the alternative country, visited it, and spoken to people living there? Would you choose it if the primary option disappeared tomorrow?

decision_factors.factor: STEM vs. non-STEM major
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines OPT length (12 vs. 29 months), H-1B eligibility window, and earning potential — the entire financial calculus and immigration timeline differ fundamentally
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether your CIP code qualifies for STEM OPT extension via the DHS STEM designated degree program list
