decision_factors.factor: Industry-specific demand gap between home and host country
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same degree can have very different market value depending on how saturated or undersupplied the field is in the target country — e.g., environmental engineering has a 420,000-person gap in China vs. mature saturation in North America
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research sector-level hiring reports (e.g., CCG海归就业报告, 猎聘大数据) for home country demand, and compare with host country employment outlook for your specific subfield

decision_factors.factor: Cultural and social integration depth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: People who cannot form genuine friendships with locals or feel culturally alien experience persistent unhappiness regardless of income level
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask honestly: do I laugh at the same jokes? Do I enjoy unstructured social time with Americans/Canadians, or do I find it hollow? Do I have close non-Chinese friends?

decision_factors.factor: Age at time of return decision
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Lifestyle habits, social network roots, and career positioning all compound with time — returning later means higher readjustment cost and less upside from China's growth trajectory
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Are you under 35? Do you still feel culturally fluid between both environments?

decision_factors.factor: Entrepreneurship feasibility by location

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: does your career ambition include founding or co-founding a company within 5 years? If yes, and you are on a work visa, the US path significantly limits this

decision_factors.factor: Trajectory vs. current state
decision_factors.why_it_matters: One commenter argues that the trend of a country's development matters more than its current snapshot — using real estate and stock market analogies to illustrate that being in the 'main upswing' phase generates more opportunity than arriving at the peak
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare directional change over decades, not just present conditions; ask whether the country is solving problems faster than it is creating them

decision_factors.factor: Personal skill level and employability in the home country job market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Returning without competitive skills leads to unemployment or underemployment — multiple commenters note high youth unemployment rates and sea-returnees earning low salaries
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly evaluate what job you could get back home, at what salary, and how long the job search would realistically take

decision_factors.factor: Spouse or partner language test score
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Adds directly to the principal applicant's CRS score; CLB 7 can add ~20 points at no cost to the primary applicant's profile
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether spouse has taken an approved test; estimate their achievable CLB level based on language background

decision_factors.factor: CRS score relative to recent draw cutoffs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A CRS score that would have cleared a draw six months ago may not clear today's draw; timing dependency means the same profile can have very different outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track the last 6-12 months of draw cutoffs on the IRCC website and compare your score to the trend, not just one draw

decision_factors.factor: Concrete Plan B viability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When return to home country is treated as pure catastrophe rather than a real alternative, it distorts all immigration-related decisions toward excessive risk aversion
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research actual job market, salary range, living conditions in home country — produce a written comparison, not a vague impression

decision_factors.factor: Physical presence in Canada at time of PGWP application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students completing their final semester remotely from abroad may face eligibility or status complications when applying for PGWP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm with IRCC guidelines or an immigration consultant whether remote completion abroad affects PGWP eligibility before the final semester begins

decision_factors.factor: Network presence in Canadian local tech community
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Referral response rates (~30%) vastly outperform cold applications (~2%), making local network quality a primary driver of job search speed and success
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count the number of Canadian-based contacts who could plausibly refer you; assess whether you are attending local meetups or events where hiring managers are present

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency or investment capacity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: TEF/TCF French scores can add 25-50+ CRS points, which is often the difference between receiving an ITA and waiting indefinitely in the Express Entry pool
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess existing French background and realistic time available to invest (estimated 6 months of focused study for meaningful score gains)

decision_factors.factor: Which stage of immigration you are currently in (OPT vs. STEM OPT vs. H-1B needed)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OPT requires nothing from the employer; STEM OPT extension requires minor paperwork and E-Verify enrollment; H-1B requires a full employer petition and legal fees — each stage changes the employer's cost and willingness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know your own visa expiration timeline and be precise about which authorization you currently hold versus what you will need

decision_factors.factor: Whether outreach targets a hiring manager vs. HR/recruiter
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Managers are motivated to solve a specific technical problem and evaluate candidates on fit; HR and recruiters apply screening criteria including sponsorship filters before a human judgment is made
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn title: does this person manage an engineering or product team? If yes, they are a manager-class target. If the title includes 'Recruiter', 'Talent', or 'HR', they are a screener

decision_factors.factor: Target role type: pure research vs. applied scientist vs. software engineering
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The PhD premium varies dramatically by role — it is strong for research scientist roles, moderate for applied scientist roles, and nearly absent for pure SWE roles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether you are targeting Research Scientist (e.g., DeepMind), Applied Scientist (e.g., Amazon), or SWE roles, and map that to whether a PhD is actually required or preferred in that role's job postings

decision_factors.factor: Availability of written documentation of sponsorship promise
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Written communications (Slack messages, emails) could support a promissory estoppel legal claim against the employer, whereas pure verbal promises offer no recourse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review all onboarding communications, Slack logs, and offer-related emails for any written reference to H-1B sponsorship

decision_factors.factor: Nature of work during gap period (freelance vs. W-2 employment)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: It is unclear from OPT rules whether freelance or consulting work counts as 'employed' for unemployment day tracking — this ambiguity can affect whether days count against the 90-day limit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask an immigration attorney whether your specific work arrangement qualifies as authorized employment under your OPT EAD

decision_factors.factor: School SEVP status and audit history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: ICE SEVP has actively shut down Day 1 CPT schools mid-operation, stranding students and invalidating their enrollment status
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether the school has faced SEVP audits or terminations; check if it appears on known Day 1 CPT school lists discussed in immigration forums

decision_factors.factor: US master's degree eligibility for master's cap pool
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Registering for the master's cap gives an additional, separate lottery entry with better odds — not utilizing it is a free missed opportunity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether degree is from a US accredited institution and qualifies under USCIS rules; consult immigration attorney

decision_factors.factor: Primary purpose classification of the employing entity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Not all university-affiliated or nonprofit organizations are automatically cap-exempt; the entity's primary purpose (research vs. medical care vs. grantmaking) determines eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the employer is a university, nonprofit research org with primary research purpose, or government research org — and for hospital systems, evaluate at the department level

decision_factors.factor: Internship-to-full-time conversion rate vs. cold application odds
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The probability gap between internship conversion (~70–85% at large tech) and cold new-grad applications (~1–5%) is large enough to materially change career and visa outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate target company conversion rates from community data or alumni networks; compare against realistic cold-application odds for your profile

decision_factors.factor: Employer-specific work authorization dependency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: On H-1B or OPT, job changes are not simple career moves — they carry immigration status risk, limiting negotiating power and career mobility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is your current authorization tied to a specific employer? What is your remaining OPT/STEM OPT runway? Do you have portability options?

decision_factors.factor: Job title and H-1B specialty occupation fit
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even winning the H-1B lottery does not guarantee staying — USCIS can deny if the job title does not demonstrate that the role requires a specialized degree that a US worker cannot fill
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your actual job duties map to a recognized specialty occupation; consult an immigration attorney before assuming an H-1B approval

decision_factors.factor: CRS score controllability

decision_factors.factor: Study permit expiry date relative to PGWP processing time

decision_factors.factor: Company size and application volume

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn applicant counts; roles with 500+ applicants on Easy Apply are low-probability; target roles at companies where personal outreach can reach a decision-maker

decision_factors.factor: Co-op or Canadian work experience prior to graduation

decision_factors.factor: Recruiter visa literacy

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of the outreach email

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Can you name one concrete thing the recipient wrote, built, or said publicly that you found useful? If not, do more research before sending

decision_factors.factor: Program prestige (ranking)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High prestige is strongly predictive for academic faculty hiring but less determinative for industry research placement, making its weight dependent on the target career track
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check recent faculty placement data for academic track; check industry placement data (internships, first jobs) for industry track — these are different metrics

decision_factors.factor: Eligibility for alternative visa statuses
decision_factors.why_it_matters: L-1, O-1, or marriage-based paths can extend legal work authorization but have strict eligibility criteria; assuming availability without verifying leads to wasted time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: L-1 requires 1+ year working abroad for a multinational employer. O-1 requires demonstrable extraordinary ability. Marriage-based requires eligible relationship. Each must be evaluated against actual circumstances

decision_factors.factor: Aggregate unemployment days on post-completion OPT
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Exceeding 90 aggregate days of unemployment technically invalidates OPT status, ending work authorization and potentially triggering unlawful presence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Maintain a personal log of all unemployment days from OPT start date; treat the counter as cumulative, never resetting

decision_factors.factor: Credit transfer or prior enrollment history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Schools that grant Day 1 CPT only to students transferring in credits or proving prior enrollment elsewhere may carry a different — potentially lower — risk profile than schools granting it unconditionally
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether CPT authorization is tied to documented prior academic work or is granted with no academic prerequisites

decision_factors.factor: Availability of cap-exempt employer options
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cap-exempt employers (universities, qualifying nonprofits) can sponsor H-1B year-round without lottery, providing a path that bypasses the lottery entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether current or target employer is a university, affiliated research institution, or nonprofit with primary research purpose; ask HR about affiliated cap-exempt entities

decision_factors.factor: Primary employer's willingness to share the employee nominally
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even when the strategy is legally viable, the primary for-profit employer may object to any nominal dual-employment arrangement, blocking the path entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have a direct conversation with the primary employer's HR and legal team early; do not assume consent

decision_factors.factor: Cumulative CPT usage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Crossing 12 cumulative months of full-time CPT permanently eliminates OPT, removing the primary post-graduation work authorization buffer used during H-1B lottery cycles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track months of full-time CPT used across all internships since starting the degree; count any partial months conservatively

decision_factors.factor: Access to mental health support and community
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Chronic immigration uncertainty is a documented stressor; individuals without support systems make worse decisions under sustained anxiety
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you have access to therapy, peer communities, or others who have navigated the same process and can provide grounded perspective?

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask honestly: is a partner, family member, or close social network present in the host country? Would you be living alone in a small town with limited community?

decision_factors.factor: Geographic location within Canada (Toronto/Vancouver vs. other cities)

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare tech job posting volume in your current city vs. Toronto/Vancouver; assess willingness and feasibility to relocate

decision_factors.factor: Existence of industry PhD co-supervision programs

decision_factors.factor: Willingness to return to school as a bridge strategy

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Weigh career stage, financial cost of degree, and likelihood of finding sponsorship during the new OPT window against the cost of lost momentum

decision_factors.factor: STEM OPT vs. standard OPT status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM OPT has a different (150-day) unemployment limit, which changes how aggressively a student needs to manage job gaps
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether you are on standard post-completion OPT or STEM OPT extension; check your EAD card and DSO records

decision_factors.factor: STEM OPT eligibility and timing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM OPT adds 24 months to OPT runway, providing up to 3 lottery attempts instead of 1; without it, a single lottery failure forces departure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm STEM-designated degree program and employer E-Verify enrollment; file STEM OPT extension before initial OPT expires

decision_factors.factor: Remaining STEM OPT runway

decision_factors.factor: Industry recruiting timeline relative to student's awareness

decision_factors.factor: Tuition-to-salary recovery ratio

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate total tuition cost divided by estimated annual savings (salary minus living costs) in each scenario; compare years-to-breakeven

decision_factors.factor: Senior IC career ceiling
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Poster acknowledged US still has better trajectory ceiling for senior individual contributor roles, though the gap is closing; this matters most for high-ambition technical career paths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the top 5 companies in your field with Canadian offices vs. US-only; assess whether the roles you aspire to in 10 years exist in the Canadian market

decision_factors.factor: SOC code accuracy and specialty occupation documentation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Misclassification under a generic SOC code (e.g., 'computer programmer') can result in denial even for legitimate specialty roles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review the specific duties of the role against DOL SOC definitions; work with attorney to build RFE-resistant specialty occupation evidence

decision_factors.factor: Timing relative to Chinese campus recruiting cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Missing the annual campus recruiting window (校招) forces candidates into social recruiting (社招), where competition is stiffer and most roles require 2+ years of experience — a gap that 1-year OPT work does not fill
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your OPT end date against Chinese campus recruiting seasons; determine whether returning mid-cycle is feasible or whether you will fall into the social recruiting pool
decision_factors._source: zhihu_出国留学后到底是否回国工作.txt

decision_factors.factor: Psychological need for achievement visibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some people need to feel their effort is visibly exceptional relative to peers; in the US this need may go unmet because success comes 'too easily' compared to peers back home
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Examine whether you derive satisfaction from the absolute level of achievement or from the competitive recognition of that achievement within a peer group
decision_factors._source: zhihu_如果你已经有了美国工作签_你会选择留美还是回国.txt

decision_factors.factor: Family proximity and emotional rootedness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple answers cite family separation and cultural identity as primary drivers of the return decision — these factors are often underweighted in financial calculations but end up dominating long-term satisfaction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: How often do you feel acute longing for family? Do you envision raising children in a Chinese-language cultural environment?
decision_factors._source: zhihu_未来应留在美国还是回国生活.txt

decision_factors.factor: Job role autonomy and decision-making involvement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The Shanghai returnee describes her US job as being a 'production machine with zero decision-making,' which caused identity erosion; China roles (especially at startups) more often place people in stretch positions beyond their current ability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: In your current or prospective US role, are you a decision-maker or an executor? Does the org structure allow people with your background to move into strategy or leadership?
decision_factors._source: zhihu_海归女硕士一枚_快毕业了是继续留在美国还是回国工作.txt

decision_factors.factor: Age at decision point and 35-year-old China tech industry cliff
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Returning to China's tech sector after 30 means facing the '35-year-old layoff curse' with a compressed runway; returning at 28 vs 34 is structurally different
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate how many years of runway you have before the 35-year threshold in Chinese tech; assess whether your role would be shielded (management, rare specialty) or exposed
decision_factors._source: zhihu_如果你已经有了美国工作签_你会选择留美还是回国.txt

decision_factors.factor: Social capital utility by profession
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In China's relationship-based society, professions that carry social resource access (doctors, teachers, bankers) command disproportionate informal status — engineers/programmers have high income but zero social resource leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Can your profession help family and friends navigate China's system (healthcare, education, finance)? Or is your value purely market-transactional?
decision_factors._source: zhihu_未来应留在美国还是回国生活.txt

decision_factors.factor: Salary comparability after cost-of-living and tax adjustment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Nominal salary comparison between US and China is misleading — $37K USD (equivalent to RMB 250K at the time of writing) is described as a low US salary, while RMB 110K is described as a low Shanghai salary; the real comparison requires local purchasing power adjustment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Convert both salaries to local median income percentile, not absolute purchasing power — what tier of life does each salary buy in each city?
decision_factors._source: zhihu_海归女硕士一枚_快毕业了是继续留在美国还是回国工作.txt

decision_factors.factor: Identity and cultural continuity for future children
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters flag that US-born or US-raised children of Chinese immigrants become culturally American — for those with strong cultural identity attachment, this is an irreversible loss
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you want your children to grow up fluent in Chinese, embedded in Chinese cultural practices? Would an ABC identity for your children feel like a loss?
